state_program_name: Licensed Home Care Services Agency (LHCSA) licensed by NYS DOH with Public Health and Health Planning Council approval (PHL Article 36; 10 NYCRR Parts 765–766); Medicaid personal care under 18 NYCRR 505.14, paid mainly through MLTC plans

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates as a Licensed Home Care Services Agency (LHCSA) in New York State. The agency is licensed by the NYS Department of Health (DOH) with approval of the Public Health and Health Planning Council (PHHPC) under Public Health Law Article 36 and 10 NYCRR Parts 765–766. It also provides Medicaid personal care under 18 NYCRR 505.14, paid mainly through Managed Long Term Care (MLTC) plans.

The manual does the following:

- Turns the regulatory requirements into written policies and step-by-step procedures that staff can follow every day.
- Gives the governing authority a basis for the oversight that 10 NYCRR §766.9 requires.
- Protects patient rights, safety and the confidentiality of records.
- Provides the written policies and procedures DOH reviews before licensure, before the pre-opening survey, and during later surveillance.
- Supports compliance with Medicaid and MLTC program rules.

The manual applies to all [AGENCY NAME] employees, contracted personnel, supervisors, committee members and governing-authority members. Where a policy and the law differ, the law controls. Report any conflict to the Administrator or governing authority so the policy can be corrected.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**1. Customize it first.** This manual is a template. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed field with agency-specific information. That includes counties served, services offered, office locations, job titles, names of designated staff, and the names of committee members. Delete or mark "not applicable" any policy for a service the agency is not approved to provide. An example is advanced home health aide (AHHA) provisions, which apply only if the agency uses AHHAs. Do not leave unexplained generic text in a submitted manual.

**2. Adopt it formally.** The governing authority must adopt the policies and any later amendments (10 NYCRR §766.1; §766.9(d)). Record the adoption in the governing-authority minutes. Show the adoption date and version on each policy.

**3. Submit it for review.** After PHHPC contingent approval, the manual goes to the DOH regional home care office. The regional office must accept it before the pre-opening survey is scheduled (DOH LHCSA Application Requirements FAQ). Submit the DOH review documents listed in the Regulatory Framework section with the manual.

**4. Use Appendix A to find the policy for any official item.** Appendix A maps every item in the official DOH checklists to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it as a table of contents when you prepare for review, for surveys, and for internal audits. If you add, remove or renumber a policy, update Appendix A at the same time.

**5. Keep it current.** Review and revise the policies as necessary (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(1)). The Quality Improvement (QI) committee must review the policies at least four times a year as part of its meetings (§766.9(l)). Personnel policies must be reviewed at least annually (§766.11(a)). The HPN coverage policy must also be reviewed at least annually (§766.9(o)). Review the manual whenever a law, regulation, DOH guidance, MLTC contract term, wage rate or reporting deadline changes. Keep dated copies of superseded versions. Record each revision, who approved it and the effective date in the revision log.

**6. Train staff on it.** All care staff must know patient rights (§766.1(b)). All employees must be oriented to the emergency plan (§766.9(c)). Orientation and in-service training are required (§766.11(i)). Train every employee on the policies that apply to their role when they are hired and again whenever a policy changes. Keep signed training records in the personnel file. Keep a current copy of the manual in the principal office, where DOH can see it (§766.12(a)(1)). Keep copies at branch offices (§766.12(a)(2)).

**7. Check the facts that change.** Wage rates, reporting windows, MLTC contract limits and supervisory-visit frequency can change. Check the primary source before relying on the figures in this manual. Where a policy says to confirm the current text or the MLTC contract, do so and document it.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Governing laws and rules

The agency is governed by the following authorities, listed by cite. The descriptions are summaries only. The policies in the manual cite the regulation text itself.

**Licensure and governance**

- **Public Health Law §3605**: A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services. PHHPC approval considers public need, character and competence, and financial resources.
- **Public Health Law §3605-b**: Annual LHCSA registration. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid.
- **10 NYCRR §765-1.2; §765-1.16**: Application review standards, including character, competence and financial feasibility, and determinations of public need.
- **10 NYCRR §700.2**: Definitions, including home care services agency and licensed home care services agency.
- **10 NYCRR §766.9**: Governing authority. This covers the emergency plan, the complaint procedure, the QI program and QI committee, management contracts, franchise agreements and HPN requirements.
- **10 NYCRR §766.10**: Contracts. Only the opening text of this section was reviewed in preparing this framework. Confirm the full text before finalizing the contract policy.
- **10 NYCRR §766.12**: Records and reports, including retention minimums and annual reports to DOH.
- **Public Health Law §3612**: Cost reporting when DOH requires it.

**Patients, care and records**

- **10 NYCRR §766.1**: Patient rights.
- **10 NYCRR §766.2**: Patient service policies and procedures, including discharge.
- **10 NYCRR §766.3**: Plan of care.
- **10 NYCRR §766.5**: Clinical supervision. Paragraph (e) applies only if the agency uses advanced home health aides.
- **10 NYCRR §766.6**: Patient care record.

**Personnel and the registry**

- **10 NYCRR §766.11**: Personnel.
- **10 NYCRR §402.6**: Criminal history record check process.
- **10 NYCRR Part 403 (§403.3, §403.5(a)(6))**: Home Care Worker Registry.
- **Public Health Law §3613**: Home care services workers (registry).
- **DOH DAL DHCBS 20-05 (1/30/2020)**: Verification of PCA, HHA and AHHA training documentation.

**Medicaid personal care and program requirements**

- **18 NYCRR §505.14(a)-(b)**: Medicaid personal care services, including scope, levels, minimum needs, assessment and authorization.
- **18 NYCRR §505.14(e)**: Personal care aide training and qualifications. Confirm the current text.
- **18 NYCRR §505.14(f)**: Nursing supervision of personal care aides. Confirm the current text and the MLTC contract, because later DOH rulemaking changed who determines the visit frequency.
- **DOH Minimum Needs Requirements (PCS/CDPAS/MLTC)**: Effective 9/1/2025.
- **DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance**: Plan of care and authorizations.
- **DOH MLTC Policy: LHCSA contract limits**: Limits on the number of LHCSAs per plan.
- **DOH Electronic Visit Verification (21st Century Cures Act, 42 USC 1396b(l))**: EVV for Medicaid personal care.
- **DOH DAL DHCBS 25-09**: Weekly HERDS reporting by LHCSAs.

**Wages**

- **Public Health Law §3614-c**: Home care worker wage parity, for Medicaid-funded home care in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester.
- **Public Health Law §3614-f**: Home care aide minimum wage.

**Audit guidance (not law)**

- **OMIG Audit Protocol: Personal Care Aides (guidance, rev. 5/11/15)**: This is audit guidance only and does not create legal requirements. The agency follows it as good practice to reduce the risk of claim disallowance.

**Review and application guidance**

- **NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool (Part B)**: The surveyor's checklist against 10 NYCRR Part 766 and the Part 403 registry provisions.
- **DOH LHCSA Application Requirements FAQ (eff. 4/1/2020)**: Covers the P&P manual and the pre-opening survey.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **NYS Department of Health, Division of Home and Community Based Services, Bureau of Home Care Licensure and Certification (with regional home care offices)** | LHCSA licensure, P&P manual review, pre-opening survey, surveillance, and license amendments (counties, services, sites) | https://www.health.ny.gov/facilities/home_care/lhcsa/ ; homecareliccert@health.ny.gov (pre-filing questions); homecareapplications@health.ny.gov (acknowledged applications and amendments); no phone number is listed in the source |
| **NYS Department of Health, Certificate of Need program (NYSE-CON)** | Electronic filing and acknowledgment of LHCSA establishment and change-of-ownership applications | cons@health.ny.gov (process); nysecon@health.ny.gov (technical); https://www.health.ny.gov/facilities/home_care/lhcsa/docs/application_requirements_faq.pdf |
| **Public Health and Health Planning Council (PHHPC)** | Approves, contingently approves or disapproves LHCSA applications on public need, character and competence, and financial feasibility; meets six times a year | https://nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/PBH/3605 ; no direct contact listed in the source |
| **NYS Department of Health, Office of Health Insurance Programs** | Medicaid personal care policy, MLTC contracting rules, fee-for-service rate setting, EVV, CDPAP | PersonalCare-Rates@health.ny.gov (rates); LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov (MLTC contract-limit exceptions); https://healthweb-back.health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/redesign/mrt90/mltc_policy/lhsca_contract_guidance.htm ; no phone number is listed in the source |
| **NYS Department of Labor** | General and home care aide minimum wage; wage parity enforcement referrals | https://dol.ny.gov/minimum-wage ; no phone or email is listed in the source |

For weekly HERDS reporting questions, DAL DHCBS 25-09 lists hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov. Complaint information that patients receive must name the DOH, as 10 NYCRR §766.1(a)(9) and §766.9(j) require. Enter the current DOH complaint contact details in the patient-rights policy and verify them at each annual review.

### Official policy checklist and application documents

DOH reviews this manual against the following official documents:

1. **LHCSA Applicant Worksheet** (NYS DOH, Division of Home and Community Based Services; "FINAL: December 2016"). This is the primary checklist. DOH says applicants should use it as a guide to assess the completeness of the P&P manual, and it must be submitted with the manual. A policy is required for each service requested. The form has no printed item numbers, so Appendix A numbers its items by section code and position.
2. **NYSDOH LHCSA P & P Review Tool, Part A (Initial Review Tool)** (revised 1-17-17). This is DOH's initial-review checklist. It covers the minimum list of policies, the format elements for each policy, the job description and P&P required for each service, and the program materials that must accompany the manual. Appendix A numbers its items A-1, A-2 and so on, in document order.
3. **NYSDOH LHCSA P & P Manual Review Tool, Part B (regulation crosswalk)** (FINAL: January 2017). The regional-office surveyor uses this tool. It reproduces the text of 10 NYCRR Parts 765, 766, 402 and 403 and grades each policy's statement, procedure and overall acceptability. Appendix A uses the document's own regulation numbering.
4. **Guidance for Developing Policies and Procedures for a Licensed Home Care Services Agency (LHCSA)** (NYS DOH, FINAL: December 2016, with Attachments A–D). It sets the submission rules and the required format for each policy. Attachment B is the sample index with a regulatory crosswalk. Attachment C lists the materials due before the pre-opening survey.

**Appendix A maps every official item from these documents to the policy in this manual that satisfies it.** Use Appendix A to confirm completeness before submission and to answer surveyor questions. The versions named above were the most recent posted on the DOH site when this manual was prepared. Check the DOH LHCSA guidance page for newer versions before submitting.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training

- **Customize.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholders and other bracketed fields before use.
- **Adopt.** The governing authority must adopt the manual and every amendment, and record this in its minutes.
- **Keep current.** Review the manual regularly and whenever the rules or guidance change. Update Appendix A with every change.
- **Train.** Train all staff on the manual, document the training, and repeat it when policies change.

citations.title: Patient rights
citations.requirement: The governing authority must adopt written patient-rights policies and procedures. Patients get their rights in writing before care starts, with documentation in the clinical record (a)(1). They get a statement of services and charges (a)(2). They are told before care how much third-party payers are expected to pay and how much the patient must pay (a)(3). Any change must be given within 30 calendar days of the agency learning of it, orally and in writing (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Other rights: be told what services will be provided and by whom (a)(4); take part in care planning (a)(5); refuse care (a)(6); complain free of reprisal (a)(7)-(9); be treated with respect (a)(10); privacy of records (a)(11); refuse advanced home health aide tasks (a)(12). Agencies must tell patients they may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management (a)(9). All care staff must know these rights (b). A legally authorized representative exercises the rights if the patient lacks capacity (c).

citations.title: Patient service policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Each service needs written policies and procedures, reviewed and revised as necessary (a)(1). Service delivery is documented in the clinical record (a)(2). Continuity: the same personnel serve the same patient where possible (a)(3). Caregivers carry current ID showing name, title, photo and agency name, returned on separation (a)(4). Written procedures cover storage, cleaning and disinfection of supplies and equipment (a)(5). Any new nursing or therapeutic service must go to the QI committee first (a)(7). A discharge plan starts before discharge (a)(8). Discharge happens only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (a)(9). "Health care services" are defined in (b) and include personal care.

citations.title: Plan of care
citations.requirement: A patient is accepted only after an RN, or a person directly supervised by an RN, determines the agency can safely and adequately meet the patient's needs (a). A plan of care is built on a professional assessment (b). It covers diagnosis, prognosis, mental status, frequency of each service, medications, treatments, diet, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential. The plan is reviewed and revised as often as needed, and at least every six months, with each review documented in the clinical record (d)(1). Staff promptly alert the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in condition (d)(2).

citations.title: Clinical supervision
citations.requirement: The governing authority must ensure sufficient trained supervisory staff (a). Supervision includes case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation, and consultation on policy. Evidence of adequate supervision (b): services delivered at the planned times and frequencies; assignment by licensure, training and demonstrated skill; prompt charting and reporting of changes in condition, adverse reactions, and problems with informal supports or the home; plans revised as needed. Aides are supervised "as appropriate" by an RN (c). In-home professional supervision occurs (d): (1) at the initial service visit or on a change in personnel, if the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, with return demonstration; (2) when a change in condition occurs, to evaluate and revise the plan; (3) to instruct the aide on required observations and written reports. Paragraph (e) covers advanced home health aides (RN home visit at least every two weeks). Not applicable unless the agency uses AHHAs.

citations.title: Patient care record
citations.requirement: Each patient has a confidential record (a) containing: identifying data; medical orders; nursing assessments; the plan of care; signed and dated progress notes after each visit or phone contact; RN supervisory reports; aide observations and activity sheets; documentation of accidents and incidents (a)(8); documentation that rights information was received (a)(9); and a discharge summary (a)(10). Records are kept securely at least 6 years after discharge and are available to DOH (b). For minors, keep until 6 years after discharge or 3 years after age 18, whichever is longer (c). If the agency closes, the governing authority must arrange storage and access and notify DOH in writing where records are kept (d). Written policies must safeguard records against loss or unauthorized access and govern use, removal and release (e).

citations.title: Governing authority
citations.requirement: The governing authority is responsible for operation and compliance with all laws (a)-(b). It must keep a current written emergency plan and orient all employees to it (c). It adopts and amends policies (d) and makes public its services, service area, charges and payment mechanisms (e). It provides an adequate office with access to patient records and prompt phone contact (f). It employs enough staff (g). It employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care (h). It accepts only patients whose needs can be met under written criteria (i). The complaint procedure (j) requires a complaint log; a written response within 15 days; notice of the right to appeal; appeal review by a governing-authority member or committee within 30 days; and notice of the right to complain to DOH. A continuous QI program is required (k). A QI committee with a consumer and health professionals meets at least four times a year (l): it reviews policies; reviews a random sample of current patients' and past-3-month discharges' records plus all complaint cases; and sends a written summary to the governing authority. Management contracts (m) and franchise agreements (n) need prior written commissioner consent; submit proposals at least 60 days before the effective date. Subdivision (o): HPN accounts, 24/7 emergency contacts, a written HPN coverage policy reviewed at least annually, and directory updates at least monthly.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: The agency may contract for patient care services. Services by arrangement require a written contract (b). Contract personnel must meet §766.11 personnel requirements (c). The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (d). Nurses or therapists under contract must coordinate and integrate with agency services (e). Subdivision (f) addresses personal care contracts with local social services districts. Only the opening text of this section was seen; confirm the full text.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (a). Aide qualifications under §700.2 must be met, and the PHL §3613(3)(a)-(f) information must be in the Home Care Registry (b). Health status is assessed before assuming duties (c). For personnel with direct patient contact (d): rubella immunity; measles immunity if born on or after 1/1/1957; TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test before employment and annually; an annual health status assessment; and influenza vaccination documentation or a mask during flu season. Identity is verified before hire (e). Employment history and references are verified before patient contact, and a criminal history record check is run as required by Part 402 (f). Personnel records hold verifications, licenses, evaluations and employment dates; health records are kept separate and confidential (g). Time and payment records are kept (h). Orientation is required, and in-service is at least 12 hours a year for HHAs, 6 for PCAs and 18 for AHHAs (i). Each position has a written job description (j). An annual performance assessment includes at least one in-home observation visit where applicable (k). A bloodborne-pathogen program (l) covers barriers, training at hire and yearly, PPE, monitoring, and an exposure-management procedure.

citations.title: Records and reports
citations.requirement: The agency must promptly submit all records and reports DOH requires (a). The principal NYS office keeps: the license, organizational documents, assumed-name certificate, patient-care contracts, governing-authority and QA bylaws, current policies, a current patient roster and a listing of all personnel (a)(1). Branch offices keep policies, a personnel list and patient records (a)(2). Retention minimums (a)(3): governing authority and committee minutes, 3 years; patient-care financial records, 3 years; personnel records, 3 years after separation; complaint and grievance records, 3 years after resolution; patient care records per §766.6. Electronic records must be secure, confidential and printable on request (b). Each year the agency furnishes DOH with statistical summaries of services and reimbursement, plus an ownership list (c).

citations.title: Definitions (home care services agency; licensed home care services agency; aide qualifications)
citations.requirement: Defines a home care services agency (a)(6) and a licensed home care services agency (a)(25) as one licensed under PHL Article 36. Per the fact-checked research, it also defines personal care aide and home health aide qualifications and training. The aide-definition text was past the truncation point in the fetch.

citations.title: Medicaid personal care services: scope, levels, minimum needs, assessment and authorization
citations.requirement: Personal care must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on assessment, delivered under a plan of care and supervised by an RN (a)(1). Eligibility requires a stable medical condition and self-direction, with the exceptions stated (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Minimum needs (a)(3)(iv): dementia or Alzheimer's needs supervision with more than one ADL; all others need limited assistance with physical maneuvering with more than two ADLs. Continuous PCS is more than 16 hours/day by more than one aide (a)(2). Live-in 24-hour PCS is one aide whose sleep is likely to be uninterrupted for 5 hours (a)(4). Level I covers nutritional and environmental support tasks only, authorized for no more than 8 hours/week (a)(5)(i). Level II adds personal care functions (a)(5)(ii)(a)(1)-(13), including medication prompting and assistance, but not administration (a)(5)(ii)(a)(10). Additional documentation is needed before authorizing more than 12 hours/day on average (a)(5)(ii)(b). Assessment (b): an independent RN assessment (RN licensed in NYS with 2+ years of home care experience), an independent medical exam and practitioner order, and plan development by the district or MMCO. Telehealth is allowed if an in-person option is offered.

citations.title: Personal care aide training and qualifications
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: a personal care aide for Medicaid needs a DOH-approved HHA program or the 40-hour PCA basic training, completed within 3 months of hire, plus 3 hours of in-service semiannually. Subdivision (e) text was not seen in the truncated fetch.

citations.title: Nursing supervision of personal care aides
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: an RN supervisory visit at least every 90 days, with a combined visit possible every six months for stable, self-directing clients. Later DOH rulemaking amended (f)(3)(vi) so the local district or MMCO determines the supervision frequency (regs.health.ny.gov summary of express terms). OMIG audit guidance says some counties require only six-month visits, so the frequency must be stated on the plan of care or in the contract. Keep a written report for each visit with the aide present. Confirm the current (f) text and the MLTC contract.

citations.title: Criminal history record check process
citations.requirement: Request a check for each prospective employee (a). An authorized person signs the DOH form, and the form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of taking the prints (b). The applicant presents two IDs, one government-issued with signature and at least one with photo (c)(1). Resubmit within 14 days of notice that prints were rejected (c)(3). Temporary approval is allowed pending results, with the §402.4 supervision (d). An expedited review request applies if the person has a prior determination or a pending submission (e).

citations.title: Home Care Worker Registry
citations.requirement: Part 403 applies to every Article 36 licensed agency. The agency must designate at least two individuals to access and enter data in the registry (§403.3(a)), and it must have policies implementing Part 403 (§403.3(b)). Only designated individuals may submit data (§403.3(c)). Within 10 business days after an aide begins providing services, the registry must be updated with employment information including the start date (§403.5(a)(6), as described in DOH DAL 19-21). A person trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 may not provide services until posted to the registry (§403.5).

citations.title: Home care services workers (registry)
citations.requirement: Establishes the Home Care Services Worker Registry and the information entered for each worker who completes a state-approved training program (name, address, gender, date of birth, program). Also provides for indicating advanced home health aide status and any limitation or revocation of that status.

citations.title: Licensure of home care services agencies
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services. PHHPC approval considers public need, character and competence, and financial resources. The application fee is $2,000 (subd. 13), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Annual LHCSA registration
citations.requirement: Annual registration since 1/1/2019. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid. The late penalty is $500 per month, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation.

citations.title: Home care worker wage parity
citations.requirement: For Medicaid-funded home care in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester: total compensation is the home care aide minimum plus a benefit portion of $2.54/hour (NYC) or $1.67/hour (Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester) from 1/1/2024. Requires an annual certification and an independently audited statement. Records are kept 10 years, per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Home care aide minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage for home care aides: $19.65 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) and $18.65 (rest of state) as of 1/1/2026. This rises to $20.00 and $19.00 on 1/1/2027.

citations.title: Cost reporting
citations.requirement: Cost reports are filed when DOH requires them: within 90 days of notice, with a 30-day correction window (2018 amendments), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Application review standards; determinations of public need
citations.requirement: Character, competence and financial feasibility standards, with working capital of at least two months of estimated operating expenses (§765-1.2). Public need rebuttable presumption of no need where 5 or more LHCSAs each actively serve 25+ patients in a county. Initial applicants must commit to serve hard-to-reach groups (§765-1.16(e)). Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: DOH MLTC Policy: LHCSA contract limits
citations.title: Licensed Home Care Services Agencies contract guidance
citations.requirement: MLTC plans may contract with no more than 1 LHCSA per 100 enrollees downstate or per 60 rest of state, with at least two LHCSAs per county accepting new enrollees. Exceptions: LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: DOH Electronic Visit Verification (21st Century Cures Act, 42 USC 1396b(l))
citations.title: EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services from 1/1/2021 (choice model: the agency picks its own vendor), with data sent to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator. It captures date, location, service, people, and start and end times. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Minimum Needs Requirements effective 9/1/2025
citations.requirement: Adults 21+ seeking PCS or CDPAS must need limited assistance with more than two ADLs (more than one ADL with supervision for dementia or Alzheimer's). It applies to initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025, and to Medicaid recipients 18+ seeking MLTC or MAP enrollment. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Weekly HERDS reporting by LHCSAs
citations.requirement: Weekly HERDS reporting includes patient census by licensed county. The window opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday 2:00 p.m. (since 6/17/2025). Contact hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool (Part B)
citations.title: DOH review tool for LHCSA P&P manuals
citations.requirement: DOH reviewers check P&P manuals against 10 NYCRR 766 (including §766.11(b)-(c)) and Part 403 registry provisions. Use it as the surveyor's checklist.

citations.title: PCA/HHA/AHHA training documentation verification
citations.requirement: When hiring aides, review the available training materials to confirm training from a DOH- or SED-approved program. The materials must include the Home Care Registry aide profile; the training certificate is included if available.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol: Personal Care Aides (guidance, rev. 5/11/15)
citations.title: Personal care audit criteria
citations.requirement: Audit guidance only; it does not create legal requirements. It describes disallowance of claims where there is no documented RN supervisory visit within 120 days before the sampled date of service. A written report is needed for each visit. The visit frequency should appear on the plan of care or in the contract.

citations.cite: DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance
citations.title: MMC guidance on NYIA, plan of care and authorizations
citations.requirement: The plan remains responsible for authorizing services and must record the level, amount, frequency and duration of authorized services in the plan of care, with notice to the enrollee. Plans coordinate with the NYIA on assessments and practitioner orders (18 NYCRR 505.14(b)(2)(iii)).

citations.title: P&P manual and pre-opening survey
citations.requirement: After PHHPC contingent approval, the P&P manual goes to the regional home care office. The regional office must accept it before the pre-opening survey. Per the fact-checked research.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Administrator and RN Director Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Governing authority members, the Administrator, the RN Director/Supervising Nurse, and all agency staff.
policies.purpose: To state who is accountable for the operation of [AGENCY NAME], a New York State licensed home care services agency (LHCSA), and to set out how the governing authority, the Administrator and the RN Director carry out their duties under 10 NYCRR §766.9 and §766.12.
policies.policy:
The governing authority of [AGENCY NAME] is legally responsible for the agency's operation and for compliance with all laws and regulations (10 NYCRR §766.9(a)-(b)). This policy meets Applicant Worksheet items WS-GA.1 through WS-GA.6 and WS-GA.8 through WS-GA.10 as follows.

WS-GA.1 (management and operation): The governing authority is responsible for the management and operation of the agency. It delegates day-to-day management to the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], but keeps ultimate responsibility.

WS-GA.2 (compliance with laws): The governing authority will ensure compliance with all applicable Federal, State and local statutes, rules and regulations, including Public Health Law Article 36 and 10 NYCRR Parts 765 and 766 (10 NYCRR §766.9(a)-(b)).

WS-GA.3 (budget): The governing authority adopts the agency's annual operating budget before the start of each fiscal year, reviews actual results against the budget at least quarterly, and approves material changes.

WS-GA.4 (policies): The governing authority adopts all written policies on the management and operation of the agency and on every service provided. It approves each amendment before the amendment takes effect (10 NYCRR §766.9(d)).

WS-GA.5 (emergency plan): The governing authority will ensure a current written emergency plan is developed and kept up to date, and that all employees are oriented to it (10 NYCRR §766.9(c)). See SAF-05 and SAF-06.

WS-GA.6 (records and reports): The governing authority will ensure that all records and reports required by the New York State Department of Health (DOH) are submitted promptly (10 NYCRR §766.12(a)). The principal New York State office keeps the records listed in §766.12(a)(1), and the agency furnishes the annual statistical summaries and ownership list required by §766.12(c). See REC-03 and REC-04.

WS-GA.8 (office): The agency maintains office facilities large enough to conduct business efficiently, with access to patient records and prompt telephone contact (10 NYCRR §766.9(f)).

WS-GA.9 (staffing): The governing authority will employ or contract for enough qualified staff to conduct the agency's business and to ensure the quality of care provided (10 NYCRR §766.9(g)). Contracted staff are governed by GOV-06.

WS-GA.10 (RN direction): The governing authority employs at least one licensed, registered professional nurse (RN) in New York State to direct and supervise all patient care services and health care activities of the agency (10 NYCRR §766.9(h)). The RN Director is [RN DIRECTOR NAME], RN license no. [RN LICENSE NUMBER].

The governing authority also accepts only patients whose needs the agency can meet under written admission criteria (10 NYCRR §766.9(i)). See SVC-02.

definitions.definition: The owner(s), board or other body with legal responsibility for the agency. The members are listed in the agency's organizational documents.
The person the governing authority appoints to manage the agency day to day.
The licensed, registered professional nurse who directs and supervises all patient care and health care activities of the agency.
A licensed home care services agency licensed under Public Health Law Article 36.
The New York State Department of Health.

procedures: Overview: The governing authority sets direction and approves policy and budget. The Administrator runs operations. The RN Director directs clinical care. Each reports to the level above on the schedule below.
The governing authority meets at least quarterly, with a quorum as set out in the organizational documents. The secretary records minutes of each meeting.

At the first meeting of each fiscal year, the governing authority adopts a written annual budget. The budget covers staffing, supplies, training, QI activities and the facility. The vote is recorded in the minutes.
The Administrator presents budget-to-actual financial reports at each quarterly meeting. The governing authority records its review and any budget amendments in the minutes.

The governing authority reviews and adopts every new policy and every amendment by recorded vote before it takes effect. The Administrator updates the policy's revision date and the manual index (see GOV-03).

The governing authority appoints the Administrator in writing. It appoints the RN Director in writing. The RN license is verified on the NYS Office of the Professions website before appointment and annually. A copy of the verification is placed in the personnel file.

The Administrator presents the governing authority with a staffing report at each quarterly meeting. It covers aide and nurse headcount, vacancies, caseload, missed visits and overtime. If staffing is not enough to meet patient needs, the governing authority approves a recruiting or intake-hold plan.

The Administrator keeps a compliance calendar of license, registration, report and training due dates. Items due include annual LHCSA registration (see GOV-02), annual policy review, QI meetings, drills and annual in-service. The Administrator reports overdue items to the governing authority at the next meeting.

The Administrator reviews the emergency plan at least annually and after each drill or real activation. The governing authority approves updates. The Administrator makes sure all employees are oriented to the plan at hire and after each change (see SAF-05, SAF-06).

The Administrator keeps the office open [OFFICE HOURS] at [ADDRESS] with a staffed telephone at [PHONE]. After-hours calls go to the on-call number with RN access. Authorized staff can reach patient records from the office at all times.

The Administrator keeps at the principal NYS office the documents listed in 10 NYCRR §766.12(a)(1). They are the license, organizational documents, assumed-name certificate, patient-care contracts, governing authority and QA bylaws, current policies, a current patient roster and a listing of all personnel. Branch offices, if any, keep policies, a personnel list and patient records.

The Administrator submits DOH-required records and reports promptly and enters each submission in the report log with the date, the report name and the staff member who sent it (see REC-04). Annual statistical summaries and the ownership list are submitted as DOH requires.

The RN Director directs and supervises all patient care. This includes approving the clinical forms, assigning RN assessments and supervision, and reviewing incidents and changes in condition (see SVC-04, SVC-09). The RN Director gives the governing authority a clinical report at each quarterly meeting.

If the RN Director position becomes vacant, the Administrator notifies the governing authority within one business day. The governing authority names an interim RN in writing within 2 business days. No patient care continues without a licensed RN directing and supervising it.
The governing authority reviews the QI committee's written summary each quarter (see GOV-04) and records the actions it takes in response.
The governing authority reviews this policy at least annually and records the review in the minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Operates and complies with all laws; adopts the budget and all policies and amendments; ensures the emergency plan, DOH reports, office, staffing and RN direction; reviews QI summaries.
Runs the agency day to day; keeps the compliance calendar and report log; keeps required documents at the principal office; manages staffing and the office; reports to the governing authority.
Directs and supervises all patient care and health care activities; keeps a current NYS RN license; reports clinical quality to the governing authority.
Follow agency policies and complete orientation to the emergency plan.

documentation: Governing authority minutes, budget and recorded votes on policy adoption and amendment
Written appointments of the Administrator and RN Director, with RN license verification
Quarterly staffing and clinical reports
Compliance calendar and DOH report submission log
Employee emergency-plan orientation records

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area, Public Information and Advertising
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, Administrator, intake and marketing staff, and anyone who communicates with the public on the agency's behalf.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a valid license, serves only the counties on the license, keeps its annual registration current, and gives the public accurate information about its services, service area, fees and accepted payers.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet item WS-GA.7: the agency will make available to the public information about the services offered (agency brochure), the geographic area served, the fees for services, and the insurances and payment sources accepted (10 NYCRR §766.9(e)).

Licensure. A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services (Public Health Law §3605). The Public Health and Health Planning Council approves a license after considering public need, the character and competence of the operators, and financial resources (PHL §3605; 10 NYCRR §765-1.2). The agency provides only the services approved on its license, and only in the counties named on it. Adding a county or a service is a license amendment (see GOV-09) and is subject to the public-need standard in 10 NYCRR §765-1.16. [AGENCY NAME] keeps the commitment it made at application to serve hard-to-reach groups (10 NYCRR §765-1.16(e)).

Registration. [AGENCY NAME] registers annually under Public Health Law §3605-b. An unregistered agency may not operate or be paid. The late penalty is $500 per month, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation. The Administrator treats the registration deadline as a critical date.

Public information. The agency brochure and website state, accurately and in plain language, the services offered, the counties served, the charges, and the payers accepted, including Medicaid managed long-term care (MLTC) plans, Medicaid fee-for-service where applicable, and private pay. The brochure is available in the office and to anyone who asks, in the languages described in CR-06.

Advertising. All advertising and marketing is truthful. It names the agency as shown on the license, advertises only services and counties actually approved, and makes no guarantees of outcomes, eligibility or payment.

definitions.definition: The counties named on the agency's license.
The written public summary of the agency's services, service area, fees and accepted payers.
The annual registration of a LHCSA required by Public Health Law §3605-b.
The populations the agency committed to serve in its application under 10 NYCRR §765-1.16(e).

procedures: Overview: The Administrator keeps the license, registration, brochure and public statements consistent with each other and with what the agency is approved to do.

The Administrator keeps the original license, the list of approved services and the list of approved counties at the principal office. A copy of the approved-counties list is posted in the intake area.

Intake staff check each referral's county of residence against the approved-counties list before accepting it. They decline or redirect referrals outside the service area and document the reason on the referral log.

The Administrator enters the annual registration due date and a 60-day advance reminder in the compliance calendar. The Administrator completes and submits registration before the due date and keeps the confirmation in the licensure file.

If registration is missed or late, the Administrator tells the governing authority within one business day, files immediately, and records the corrective action and any $500-per-month penalty. The agency does not provide or bill for services while unregistered.

The Administrator prepares the agency brochure. It lists services (as approved on the license), counties, hours, the 24-hour contact number [PHONE], charges, accepted payers and the complaint process.
The Administrator lists the charges for each private-pay service, including any minimum hours. The charge schedule matches the Service Agreement (see CR-02).

The governing authority approves the brochure and any change to charges. The Administrator reviews the brochure at least annually and within 30 days of any change to services, counties, charges or payers.
Intake staff give the current brochure to every inquirer, and give it to each patient at admission with the admission packet.
The agency posts or publishes the brochure on its website. The Administrator checks the website at least quarterly against the brochure and the license.
Before any advertisement, flyer, social media post or website text is used, the Administrator reviews it for accuracy against the license. The Administrator keeps a dated copy in the marketing file.
Staff who are asked about services outside the license or outside approved counties say that the agency cannot provide them. They refer the inquirer to the Administrator.
Before the agency begins serving an additional county or service, the Administrator follows GOV-09 and does not advertise it until the amendment is approved.
The Administrator reports to the governing authority at each quarterly meeting on license status, registration status and any marketing complaints.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the brochure and charges; ensures the agency operates only under its license and registration.
Maintains the license and registration, compliance calendar, brochure, website and advertising review.
Check service area, provide the brochure, and decline referrals outside the license.
Confirms that clinical services described in public materials match approved services.

documentation: License, list of approved services and counties, and annual registration confirmations
Compliance calendar entries
Dated copies of the brochure, website text and advertisements, with approval dates
Referral log showing out-of-area referrals declined
Governing authority minutes recording approval of brochure and charges

policies.title: Policy Manual Format, Index, Document Control and Required Program Materials
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Director, governing authority and all staff who write, revise or use agency policies.
policies.purpose: To set one format for every policy, keep the Policy and Procedure Manual indexed and under document control, and make sure the manual and program materials contain what DOH reviewers check.
policies.policy:
The governing authority adopts and amends written policies (10 NYCRR §766.9(d)). Each service has written policies and procedures that are reviewed and revised as necessary (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(1)), and personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (10 NYCRR §766.11(a)). After PHHPC contingent approval, the manual goes to the DOH regional home care office. The regional office must accept it before the pre-opening survey (DOH LHCSA Application Requirements FAQ). DOH reviewers use the LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool to check the manual. This policy meets Review Tool items A-1 through A-7 as follows.

A-1 (Index/Table of Contents). The manual has an index listing every policy by name, policy number and initial or revision date, with the regulation each policy cites. Pages are numbered correctly. The agency name appears exactly as on the PHHPC-approved application on every page: [AGENCY NAME].

A-2 (job description and policy for each approved service). The agency has a job description and a policy and procedure for each service PHHPC approved. A service matrix in the manual lists these services as Approved or Not Approved: Nursing; Home Health Aide; Personal Care Aide; Physical Therapy; Occupational Therapy; Respiratory Therapy; Speech/Language Pathology; Audiology; Medical Social Work; Physician Services; Nutrition; Homemaker; Housekeeper; and Medical Supply, Equipment and Appliances. For this agency, the approved services are [LIST OF SERVICES APPROVED BY PHHPC, e.g., Nursing, Home Health Aide, Personal Care Aide]. A job description and a policy exist for each approved service. The agency provides no service marked Not Approved. A new nursing or therapeutic service goes to the QI committee before it starts (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(7); see GOV-04) and is added by license amendment (see GOV-09).

A-3 (minimum policy set, part 1). The manual contains a policy and procedure for each of: Patient Rights (CR-01); Complaint Procedure (CR-03); Admission (SVC-02); Discharge/Discharge Planning (SVC-15); Plan of Care (SVC-06); Assessment (SVC-05); Medical Orders (SVC-07); Clinical Supervision (SVC-09); and Clinical Records (REC-01).

A-4 (minimum policy set, part 2). The manual contains a policy and procedure for each of: Quality Assurance and Quality Improvement Program (GOV-04); Contract Procedure (GOV-06); Health Commerce System (GOV-07); Personnel (PER-01); Criminal History Record Check (PER-04); Home Care Registry (PER-03); Infection Control and Bloodborne Pathogens (SAF-03, SAF-04); Change of Ownership and Amendment of License (GOV-08, GOV-09); Governing Authority (GOV-01); and Emergency Preparedness (SAF-05, SAF-06). Other policies in the manual cover other applicable areas.

A-5 (program materials). The agency keeps these materials ready for submission: the Emergency Preparedness Plan (SAF-05); the Admission/Start of Care packet (SVC-02, CR-02); the agency brochure (GOV-02); the Patient Bill of Rights (CR-01); clinical record forms (assessment/reassessment, plan of care, physician orders, aide activity sheet and aide care plan, see REC-01, SVC-06, SVC-07, SVC-08); and personnel record forms (PER-08). Administrative items on the review tool, such as the Federal Tax ID number and the QI committee member names and titles, are kept by the Administrator and are not policy content.

A-6 (required elements of each policy). Every policy in this manual shows: the agency name as on the PHHPC-approved application; a discrete policy number; a title; a policy statement/purpose; the policy date and revision date; a page number in 'page x of y' form; the authority (statute, regulation and agency policy); the application (who or what the policy applies to); the responsible party (title and contact information); terminology unique to the policy; and cross-references to other agency policies.

A-7 (procedure). Every policy includes a step-by-step procedure with, as appropriate, an overview; the skills and materials needed; a logical sequence of steps and sub-steps in the order they occur; and diagrams, forms or examples where they help.

definitions.definition: The governing authority-approved collection of all written agency policies and procedures.
The process that tracks each policy's number, version, dates, approvals and distribution so staff use only current versions.
The NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool that DOH reviewers use.
The DOH regional office that accepts the manual and conducts the pre-opening survey.

procedures: Overview: The Administrator owns the manual. Each policy is drafted on the standard template, reviewed by the RN Director for clinical content, approved by the governing authority, indexed, and distributed.

Draft each policy on the standard template with these header fields: agency name as on the PHHPC approval, policy number, title, policy date, revision date, page 'x of y', responsible party and contact information.

Include in each policy the purpose, policy statement, authority, application, terminology, procedure and cross-references (A-6, A-7). Write the procedure in numbered steps in the order they happen, naming who does what, by when, and where it is documented.
The RN Director reviews every clinical policy. The Administrator reviews every administrative policy. Both sign and date the review sheet.
The governing authority approves each new policy and each revision by recorded vote (10 NYCRR §766.9(d)). The Administrator then enters the approval date as the policy date or revision date.

The Administrator updates the index immediately. For each policy it lists the name, number, initial and latest revision date, and the regulation cited. The Administrator checks that page numbers and the agency name are correct throughout.

The Administrator maintains the service matrix and confirms that a job description (see PER-01) and a policy exist for each service PHHPC approved (A-2). This check is repeated whenever a service is added or removed.

Before filing the manual after contingent approval, the Administrator completes a self-audit with the Review Tool. The audit confirms the A-3 and A-4 policies exist, that program materials (A-5) are attached, and that each policy has the A-6 elements and an A-7 procedure. The Administrator and RN Director sign the audit.

The Administrator submits the manual to the DOH regional home care office after PHHPC contingent approval. The Administrator keeps the submission date and the regional office's acceptance. The agency does not schedule the pre-opening survey until the manual is accepted.

Review every policy at least annually. Personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (10 NYCRR §766.11(a)). The Administrator also revises any policy when a regulation, DOH guidance or an agency practice changes (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(1)). The QI committee reviews policies on each of its meetings' schedule (see GOV-04).

When a policy is revised, the Administrator keeps the superseded version in the archive for at least 3 years and marks it 'Superseded'. The Administrator removes outdated copies from the working manual.

The Administrator keeps the current manual at the principal office and available to all staff, electronically with a printed copy at the office. Staff sign an acknowledgment of the manual at hire and after material revisions.

Before a new nursing or therapeutic service is begun, the Administrator submits the proposal to the QI committee (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(7)), and the governing authority adopts the policy and job description for it.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts and amends all policies; approves the manual before submission.
Owns the manual, index, service matrix, version control, annual review and the submission to the regional office.
Reviews clinical policies and clinical forms; co-signs the Review Tool self-audit.
Reviews policies as part of its quarterly work and reviews proposed new nursing or therapeutic services.
Use only the current version and sign the manual acknowledgment.

documentation: Approved manual with index/table of contents and service matrix
Policy review sheets and governing authority approval minutes
Review Tool self-audit
Submission to and acceptance from the regional home care office
Archive of superseded policies
Staff manual acknowledgments

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QI Committee)
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, QI committee members, Administrator, RN Director and all staff and services of the agency.
policies.purpose: To run a continuous quality assessment and improvement program at [AGENCY NAME] that covers all staff, all services and all aspects of care, and to report its findings to the governing authority.
policies.policy:
The governing authority requires a continuous quality improvement (QI) program (10 NYCRR §766.9(k)) and a QI committee that includes a consumer and health professionals and meets at least four times a year (10 NYCRR §766.9(l)). This policy meets Applicant Worksheet items WS-GA.19 through WS-GA.28 as follows.

WS-GA.19: The agency has a quality assessment and improvement program that involves all staff, and its plan includes all aspects of care delivered.

WS-GA.20: The governing authority appoints a QI committee that includes at least one consumer (a patient, family member or patient representative who is not an employee) and health professionals, including the RN Director.

WS-GA.21: QI activities are continuous and cover every program and service the agency provides.

WS-GA.22: The committee meets at least four times a year. The agency's schedule is once each calendar quarter.

WS-GA.23: The committee establishes and oversees standards of care and tracks them with measurable indicators.

WS-GA.24: The committee reviews the agency's policies pertaining to health care services.

WS-GA.25: The committee conducts a clinical record review of a random sample of current patients' records.

WS-GA.26: The committee conducts a clinical record review of records of patients discharged within the previous 3 months.

WS-GA.27: The committee reviews all complaint and grievance cases (see CR-03).

WS-GA.28: The committee prepares and submits a written summary of its findings to the governing authority.

Any new nursing or therapeutic service is presented to the QI committee before it begins (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(7)).

definitions.definition: The governing authority-appointed committee that carries out the QI program. It includes a consumer and health professionals.
A committee member who receives or has received home care services, or is a family member or representative of a patient, and is not an agency employee or owner.
Written, measurable expectations for service quality and safety, such as the timeliness of RN supervisory visits and plan-of-care updates.
A measurable item tracked over time, such as the missed visit rate, the incident rate or the complaint response time.

procedures: Overview: The committee meets each quarter, reviews fixed agenda items, records findings and corrective actions, and reports in writing to the governing authority.

The governing authority appoints committee members in writing. They include the RN Director, at least one other health professional, the Administrator or designee, and at least one consumer member. The Administrator keeps the roster with names and titles.

The Administrator schedules four meetings a year, one per quarter, at the start of the calendar year. If a meeting is missed, the Administrator reschedules it within 30 days and informs the governing authority.
The Administrator sends the agenda and review materials to members at least 5 days before each meeting.

Standing agenda item 1 (policies, WS-GA.24): The committee reviews the policies tied to health care services scheduled for that quarter, so that every health care policy is reviewed at least annually. It recommends revisions to the governing authority.

Standing agenda item 2 (current patient records, WS-GA.25): The RN Director draws a random sample of current patients' clinical records. The sample is at least 10% of active patients and no fewer than [SAMPLE MINIMUM, e.g., 10] records, across all services and all counties. Reviewers use a standard audit tool that checks the assessment, plan of care, orders, aide care plan, task documentation, RN supervisory visits, incident follow-up and patient rights documentation.

Standing agenda item 3 (discharged patient records, WS-GA.26): The RN Director reviews a random sample of records of patients discharged in the previous 3 months. Reviewers check the discharge plan, the 48-hour notice to the authorized practitioner, consultation with the patient and staff, and discharge instructions (see SVC-15).

Standing agenda item 4 (complaints, WS-GA.27): The committee reviews every complaint and grievance case since the last meeting, including the complaint log, response times, outcomes and appeals. It identifies trends.

Standing agenda item 5 (standards of care, WS-GA.23): The committee reviews indicators including missed visits, late RN supervisory visits, EVV exceptions, incidents, change-in-condition reports, infection control events, patient satisfaction and staff turnover. It sets or revises the standard for each indicator.
For each deficiency, the committee assigns a corrective action, a responsible person and a due date. It follows up at the next meeting until the action is closed and effective.
Any proposed new nursing or therapeutic service is brought to the committee before it starts (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(7)). The committee votes on its recommendation and records it.
The Administrator records minutes at every meeting, covering attendance, items reviewed, findings, actions and votes.
Within 14 days of each meeting, the committee chair and RN Director sign a written summary of findings and recommendations and send it to the governing authority (WS-GA.28).
The governing authority reviews each summary at its next meeting, decides what action to take and records the decision in its minutes.
The Administrator keeps QI records under REC-03 and keeps patient identifiers out of the committee's summary reports wherever possible (see CR-04).
The committee reviews this QI plan at least annually to confirm it covers all staff, all services and all aspects of care (WS-GA.19, WS-GA.21).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the committee; receives and acts on written summaries; ensures continuous QI for all services.
Runs the meetings and signs the written summary.
Brings the patient perspective to the review of standards, complaints and satisfaction.
Draws the record samples, leads the clinical review, and follows up on corrective actions.
Schedules meetings, keeps the roster, minutes and reports; follows up on administrative actions.

documentation: QI committee roster with names, titles and consumer member identified
Agendas, minutes and attendance for at least four meetings a year
Completed record audit tools for current and discharged patients
Complaint review summaries and indicator reports
Written summary of findings to the governing authority and the governing authority's response
Corrective action tracking log

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, Administrator, compliance officer, billing and scheduling staff, RNs, aides and contractors.
policies.purpose: To prevent, detect and correct fraud, waste and abuse, and to make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services that were authorized, actually delivered and documented.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid, MLTC plans and private payers only for services that were authorized, delivered as planned and documented. The agency supports this with a compliance program. It names a compliance officer, trains staff, runs a reporting hotline and forbids retaliation.

Whether the Medicaid compliance-program requirement (Social Services Law §363-d and 18 NYCRR Part 521) applies to this agency has not been verified. The Administrator will confirm this with counsel or the Office of the Medicaid Inspector General (OMIG). This policy is written to the standard of that program either way.

Billable service. Medicaid personal care must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on an assessment, delivered under a plan of care, and supervised by an RN (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(1)). The agency bills only within the authorized level and hours. Level I (nutritional and environmental support tasks only) is authorized for no more than 8 hours a week. Level II adds personal care functions, including medication prompting and assistance but not administration. Additional documentation is needed before authorizing more than 12 hours a day on average (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(5)). Each billed visit is supported by an electronic visit verification (EVV) record (42 USC 1396b(l); see SVC-13), the aide activity sheet and, as due, a documented RN supervisory visit. OMIG may disallow claims that lack a documented RN supervisory visit.

False claims. Knowingly submitting or causing a false claim for payment is prohibited under the federal False Claims Act (31 USC 3729). Overpayments are reported and returned promptly.

Cost reports. The agency files cost reports when DOH requires them: within 90 days of notice, with a 30-day correction window (Public Health Law §3612).

definitions.definition: The person the governing authority designates to run the compliance program, reporting to the Administrator and the governing authority.

Fraud is an intentional false statement or claim for payment. Waste is overuse or misuse of resources. Abuse is practice that results in unnecessary cost or payment for services that were not needed or not provided.
Any payment received by the agency to which it was not entitled.
Electronic visit verification: the electronic record of the date, location, service, people and start and end times of a Medicaid personal care visit.
The NYS Office of the Medicaid Inspector General.

procedures: Overview: The agency prevents billing errors through pre-bill checks, finds problems through audits and hotline reports, and corrects them through repayment and retraining.

The governing authority appoints a compliance officer in writing, [COMPLIANCE OFFICER NAME], with direct access to the governing authority. The Administrator may be named compliance officer only if the governing authority records why this is appropriate for an agency of this size.

The Administrator asks counsel or OMIG whether SSL §363-d and 18 NYCRR Part 521 apply to the agency and records the answer in the compliance file within 60 days of licensure. The agency follows the steps below regardless of the answer.

The compliance officer issues a written code of conduct. Staff receive it at hire and sign it. They receive compliance training at hire and annually, covering billing rules, EVV, documentation, false claims and how to report concerns.

The agency keeps a reporting hotline, [COMPLIANCE HOTLINE PHONE], and an anonymous option. Staff, patients and contractors may report concerns without fear. Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is prohibited and is grounds for discipline up to termination.

Before each billing cycle, billing staff match each claim line to: an active authorization (type, level and hours); a completed EVV record; and a signed aide activity sheet. They hold any claim line that lacks one of these.

Billing staff do not bill hours above what is authorized, or for tasks outside the authorized level. For Level I cases they confirm that no personal care functions are billed. For cases averaging more than 12 hours a day they confirm that the required additional documentation is in the record.

The RN Director checks monthly that each required RN supervisory visit is documented and filed (see SVC-10). Claims for periods without a required supervisory visit go to the compliance officer for review before billing.

The compliance officer reviews EVV exceptions (manual edits, late entries, missing locations) monthly. Unexplained edits, duplicate or overlapping visits, or visits at times an aide could not have been present are investigated within 10 business days.

Before hire and monthly, the compliance officer checks employees, contractors and vendors against the federal OIG exclusion list and the OMIG exclusion list. The agency does not employ or bill for excluded persons. Results are logged.

The compliance officer performs a quarterly audit of a random sample of paid claims, comparing them to the authorization, EVV record, activity sheet, plan of care and supervisory visit. Findings go to the Administrator and the QI committee.

When an overpayment or billing error is found, the compliance officer quantifies it, stops further billing of the same error, reports it to the payer and returns the funds promptly. The compliance officer documents the date discovered, the amount and the corrective action.

When the compliance officer suspects fraud, such as billing for visits not performed, the compliance officer reports it to the governing authority and counsel and secures the records. Counsel advises on external reporting.

Upon DOH notice that a cost report is due, the Administrator logs the due date (90 days from notice), prepares the report with the agency's accountant, has the governing authority review it, files it on time and responds to any correction request within the 30-day window (Public Health Law §3612).
The compliance officer reports to the governing authority at each quarterly meeting on hotline calls, audit results, repayments and training completion. The governing authority records its review.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the compliance officer, oversees the program and acts on quarterly reports.
Runs training, the hotline, exclusion checks, audits, investigations and repayments.
Ensures billing controls and cost report filing; supports corrective action.
Ensures RN supervisory visits and clinical documentation that support billing.
Apply pre-bill checks and bill only supported, authorized services.
Document truthfully, report concerns and never falsify visit or time records.

documentation: Compliance officer appointment and the SSL §363-d applicability determination
Signed code of conduct and training records
Hotline log and investigation files
Exclusion check logs
Pre-bill check records and quarterly audit reports
Overpayment and repayment records
Cost reports, filing dates and DOH correspondence
Governing authority minutes recording compliance reports

policies.title: Contracts and Services by Arrangement
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, Administrator, RN Director, and any individual or organization providing services to [AGENCY NAME] patients under contract.
policies.purpose: To make sure that any patient care service [AGENCY NAME] provides through a contract is under a written agreement, is supervised and evaluated, and meets the same standards as services provided by agency employees.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] may contract for patient care services. Services by arrangement require a written contract (10 NYCRR §766.10(b)). The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (10 NYCRR §766.10(d)). Nurses or therapists under contract coordinate and integrate their services with the agency's services (10 NYCRR §766.10(e)). The governing authority or operator is responsible for ensuring that each written contract meets Applicant Worksheet items WS-CON.1 through WS-CON.6, as follows.

WS-CON.1: The contract states the services to be provided.

WS-CON.2: The contract states how the services will be supervised and evaluated.

WS-CON.3: The contract states the charges and other financial arrangements.

WS-CON.4: The contract has a 'notwithstanding clause' stating that, notwithstanding the contract, the agency retains responsibility for the adequacy of services to its patients and for compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

WS-CON.5: The contract has provisions for indemnification between the agency and the contract provider.

WS-CON.6: The contract states that contract staff must meet all personnel requirements of 10 NYCRR §766.11 (10 NYCRR §766.10(c)), including aide qualifications and Home Care Registry entries, health status, immunity and TB screening, identity and reference verification, criminal history record check, orientation, in-service training, a written job description and bloodborne pathogen training.

Special contracts. Contracts for personal care services with local social services districts are addressed in 10 NYCRR §766.10(f), and managed long-term care plan contracts are handled under SVC-17 and GOV-05. Management and franchise contracts require the commissioner's prior written consent, with the proposal submitted at least 60 days before the effective date (10 NYCRR §766.9(m)-(n); see GOV-08).

definitions.definition: A patient care service the agency delivers through a contractor rather than through its own employees.
Individuals who provide care to agency patients under a contract and are not agency employees.
A contract term stating that the agency remains responsible for the adequacy of services despite the contract.
A promise by one party to protect the other from loss or liability arising from the first party's acts.

procedures: Overview: The Administrator identifies a need for contracted services, checks the contractor, drafts and signs a compliant written contract, onboards contract staff as if they were employees, and monitors the contractor.

Before using any contractor for patient care, the Administrator documents the need and gets the governing authority's approval. If the service is new nursing or therapeutic service, it goes to the QI committee first (see GOV-04).
The Administrator checks the contractor's license or registration (where applicable), insurance, exclusion status, and reputation, and keeps the findings in the contract file.
The Administrator drafts a written contract using the agency's template before any services start. Counsel reviews it before signature.
Services (WS-CON.1): The contract lists each service, the patients or populations covered, the hours or visit frequency and the contractor's response times.

Supervision and evaluation (WS-CON.2): The contract states which agency RN supervises the contractor's work, how often the work is observed or reviewed, how the contractor's performance is evaluated at least annually, and how contract staff coordinate with the agency's plan of care (10 NYCRR §766.10(e)).
Charges (WS-CON.3): The contract states rates, how and when invoices are submitted and paid, and the documents needed to support payment (activity sheets, EVV records, visit notes).

Notwithstanding clause (WS-CON.4): The contract includes language that, notwithstanding the contract, the agency retains responsibility for the adequacy of services provided to its patients and for compliance with all laws, and that nothing in the contract reduces that responsibility.

Indemnification (WS-CON.5): The contract includes indemnification provisions running both ways between the agency and the contractor, and requires the contractor to carry liability insurance at stated minimums, with proof on file.

Personnel requirements (WS-CON.6): The contract requires the contractor to supply, before any contract staff member has patient contact, proof of every requirement in 10 NYCRR §766.11 that applies to the role. The agency may run the verifications itself. The RN Director or designee reviews the proof and signs off before the first assignment (see PER-02, PER-03, PER-04, PER-05, PER-06).

The contract states that the contractor must follow agency policies on patient rights, confidentiality, incident reporting, infection control and abuse reporting. Contract staff are oriented to these before the first visit.

The governing authority approves the contract, and the Administrator and contractor sign. The signed original is kept at the principal office (10 NYCRR §766.12(a)(1) requires patient care contracts to be kept there).
The RN Director monitors contract services at least quarterly with record review and, for aide or direct-care contractors, in-home observation. Results are reported to the QI committee.
The Administrator checks contract staff credentials and exclusion status annually. If a contract staff member does not meet requirements, services by that person stop immediately.

The Administrator confirms the full current text of 10 NYCRR §766.10 against this policy at each annual review. The Administrator also checks whether any proposed arrangement is a management or franchise contract. If it is, no agreement is signed until the Administrator submits the proposal to the commissioner at least 60 days before the proposed effective date and written consent is received (10 NYCRR §766.9(m)-(n)).
To end a contract, the Administrator gives the written notice the contract requires. The RN Director arranges for continuity of care for affected patients so no patient loses services (see SVC-12).

responsibilities.duty: Approves contracts and ensures each contract has the required terms; seeks commissioner consent for management or franchise contracts.
Drafts, signs and files contracts; verifies insurance and personnel proof; manages renewals and terminations.
Supervises and evaluates contracted clinical services; coordinates contract nurses and therapists with the agency's services; signs off on contract staff readiness.
Delivers services per the contract and agency policies and supplies all required personnel documentation.

documentation: Signed contract and governing authority approval
Contractor license, insurance and exclusion check
Contract staff personnel verifications and RN sign-off
Orientation records for contract staff
Quarterly monitoring and annual evaluation of the contractor
Any commissioner consent correspondence for management or franchise contracts

policies.title: Health Commerce System (HCS) Account and Communication Directory
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, Administrator, Director of Patient Services, Emergency Response Coordinator, HCS Coordinator, CHRC Authorized Person, Home Care Registry designees and all staff who receive or answer DOH communications
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] can always receive, and promptly answer, official communications, alerts, surveys and data requests from the NYS Department of Health (DOH) and local health departments through the Health Commerce System (HCS, referred to in 10 NYCRR 766.9(o) as the HPN), and that DOH can always reach the agency, including after hours.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] will keep an active HCS account for each agency it operates, as required by 10 NYCRR 766.9(o). The account will be checked every business day, will be covered throughout the agency's hours of operation, and will be staffed well enough to answer DOH requests quickly. The 24/7 facility contact and the Office of the Administrator information will be kept current. The HCS communication directory will be reviewed and updated at least monthly. The written HCS coverage policy (this policy) will be reviewed at least annually. This policy meets the following items on the Applicant Worksheet (p.9), Health Commerce System policy/procedure:
- WS-HCS.1: the agency will obtain an HCS account for each agency operated.
- WS-HCS.2: a sufficient number of knowledgeable staff will be available to maintain and keep current the account (the HCS Coordinator and at least one trained backup).
- WS-HCS.3: the system will be accessed daily.
- WS-HCS.4: the agency will have consistent coverage within its hours of operation.
- WS-HCS.5: the agency will have sufficient staff to ensure rapid response to requests for information from the State or local DOH.
- WS-HCS.6: information will be current for the 24/7 Facility Contact and the Office of the Administrator.
- WS-HCS.7: the agency's communication directory will be kept current and updated, at least monthly.
- WS-HCS.8: the agency will assign the Administrator; Director of Patient Services; Emergency Response Coordinator; HCS Coordinator; CHRC Authorized Person; and Home Care Registry Agency Updater and Viewer (at least two registry designees under 10 NYCRR Part 403).

definitions.definition: The secure DOH web portal used for official communications, alerts, surveys, directory maintenance and data reporting. 10 NYCRR 766.9(o) refers to it as the HPN.
The HCS listing of the agency's contacts, including the 24/7 facility contact and the Office of the Administrator, which DOH uses to reach the agency.
The person or number staffed at all hours, including nights, weekends and holidays, who can receive DOH emergency notices and act on them.
The staff member who manages the agency's HCS account, assigns and removes user roles, and keeps the directory current.
A person the agency designates under 10 NYCRR 403.3(a) to access and enter data in the Home Care Worker Registry. The agency must designate at least two.
