The patient or legally authorized representative signs an informed consent form before the first service. If the patient lacks capacity, the RN verifies and records the representative's authority. The consent form is filed in the clinical record. A copy goes to the patient.

If the patient declines to consent, or withdraws consent at any time, services do not begin or are stopped. The RN documents the refusal and any risks explained, and informs the referral source as the law permits.

If the RN determines that the patient's needs cannot be safely and adequately met (for example, nursing or skilled needs beyond the agency's services, unsafe home, no staff available, outside the licensed counties, or required hours exceeding capacity), the agency does not accept the patient.

For each non-acceptance, the RN or Administrator documents the reason, tells the patient or referral source promptly and in writing, and helps refer the person to other providers, the MLTC plan or the local social services district, as appropriate. The written notice does not state discriminatory reasons.
When a patient is accepted, the RN Director assigns an aide on the basis of licensure, training and demonstrated skill (see SVC-09) and the scheduler confirms the start of care (see SVC-12).
If a patient's needs change after admission such that the agency can no longer safely meet them, the RN follows SVC-14 and SVC-15 to modify the plan, transfer or discharge with proper notice.
The QI Committee reviews acceptance and non-acceptance decisions, including the reasons and any trends, at least quarterly (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts, reviews and amends the written admission criteria and ensures only appropriate patients are accepted.
Ensures admission procedures are followed, reviews declined referrals and ensures adequate staffing before acceptance.
Directs RN determinations of whether needs can be met safely and adequately and signs acceptance decisions.

responsibilities.role: RN (or person directly supervised by an RN)
responsibilities.duty: Evaluates the referral, completes the determination, obtains informed consent and gives rights and charges information.
Logs referrals, gathers orders and authorizations, schedules admissions and sends notices of non-acceptance.

documentation: Referral and intake form
Admission determination signed by the RN (or supervised person and RN)
Practitioner order and authorization
Signed rights acknowledgment and statement of services and charges
Signed informed consent
Notices of non-acceptance and referral-out records with reasons
QI review of admissions

policies.title: Client Intake, Medicaid Eligibility, Independent Assessment and Minimum Needs
policies.applies_to: Intake staff, RNs, the RN Director, schedulers and billing staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure Medicaid personal care is provided only after the required independent assessment, medical exam, practitioner order and authorization, that minimum-needs requirements are checked, and that staff provide only the hours and level the plan authorizes.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides Medicaid personal care only when the requirements of 18 NYCRR §505.14 are met. Personal care must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on assessment, delivered under a plan of care and supervised by an RN (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(1)). Medicaid personal care requires an independent RN assessment (an RN licensed in New York State with at least two years of home care experience), an independent medical exam and a practitioner order. Plan development is by the district or by the MLTC plan/MMCO (18 NYCRR §505.14(b)). Telehealth assessment is allowed if an in-person option is offered. For adults 21 and older, minimum needs require limited assistance with more than two ADLs, or more than one ADL with supervision for dementia or Alzheimer's (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(3)(iv); DOH Minimum Needs Requirements). These requirements apply to initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025, and to Medicaid recipients age 18 and older seeking MLTC or MAP enrollment. The plan remains responsible for authorizing services and must record the level, amount, frequency and duration in the plan of care, with notice to the enrollee (DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance). Agency staff work only the authorized hours. Private-pay intake follows the RN assessment under SVC-05. Acceptance is always subject to the RN determination in 10 NYCRR §766.3(a) and SVC-02. The agency also supports person-centered planning and the patient's choice, consistent with the home and community-based services rule at 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: The assessment of a Medicaid applicant or enrollee's needs by an RN who is independent of the agency, licensed in New York State and has at least two years of home care experience, as 18 NYCRR §505.14(b) requires; in managed care, coordinated with the NYIA and the plan.
The New York Independent Assessor, which performs the independent assessment and practitioner order coordination under DOH guidance.
A managed long term care plan or other Medicaid managed care organization that authorizes and pays for the enrollee's services.
The level of ADL need required to qualify for personal care: limited assistance with physical maneuvering with more than two ADLs, or for dementia/Alzheimer's, supervision with more than one ADL.
Activity of daily living, such as bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, mobility and eating.
The plan's or district's determination of the level (I or II), amount, frequency and duration of services that may be provided and billed.
Continuous PCS is more than 16 hours a day by more than one aide; live-in 24-hour PCS is one aide whose sleep is likely to be uninterrupted for five hours (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(2), (a)(4)).

procedures: At first contact, the intake coordinator asks the payer source. If the person is Medicaid-eligible, the intake coordinator records the Medicaid ID, the MLTC plan or district, the referral source and the stage of the assessment.

For an MLTC or managed care enrollee, the intake coordinator contacts the plan's care manager and requests the authorization, plan of care, independent assessment results, practitioner order and expected start date. The agency does not start care on a verbal promise alone (see SVC-17).

The intake coordinator confirms that the file includes: (a) the independent RN assessment; (b) the independent medical exam; (c) the practitioner order; and (d) the district or plan authorization of the level, amount, frequency and duration. Missing items are requested in writing and the date of request is documented.

The RN reviews the independent assessment to confirm that minimum needs are documented: for adults 21 and over, limited assistance with more than two ADLs, or more than one ADL with supervision for dementia or Alzheimer's. This applies to initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025. For persons under 21 or in other categories, the RN asks the plan or district to confirm the applicable rule.

If the paperwork does not show that minimum needs are met, the agency does not begin personal care. The RN Director notifies the plan or district in writing and the intake coordinator informs the patient. The agency does not tell the patient how to answer assessment questions or in any way coach the outcome.

The RN checks that the authorized level is consistent with the tasks needed: Level I (nutritional and environmental support only, no more than 8 hours a week) or Level II (personal care functions, including medication prompting and assistance but not administration) (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(5)). If the authorization is for continuous or live-in care, or over 12 hours a day on average, the RN confirms that the required additional documentation is in the file before service starts.

The RN completes the agency's own professional assessment (see SVC-05) and the safety determination under 10 NYCRR §766.3(a) and SVC-02. The agency's assessment does not replace the independent assessment and does not change the authorized hours.

The RN builds the agency's plan of care from the professional assessment and the authorization, consistent with the plan of care developed by the district or plan (see SVC-06). The plan records the level, amount, frequency and duration of authorized services, as DOH guidance requires.

The scheduler enters only the authorized hours and tasks into the schedule and EVV system (see SVC-12 and SVC-13). Staff do not provide, and the agency does not bill for, hours beyond authorization. If the patient wants more hours, the RN Director refers the request to the plan or district.

If the RN finds that the authorized hours or level do not meet the patient's needs, or that the needs have changed, the RN notifies the plan or district promptly in writing, and documents the notification and response (see SVC-14 and SVC-17). Care continues at the authorized level while the request is pending, unless unsafe.

The RN Director tracks reassessment due dates for each Medicaid patient. The agency cooperates with the plan or district for each reassessment and gives the assessor and the patient access as needed. Reassessments on or after 9/1/2025 are checked for the minimum needs requirement.

If a patient is found not to meet minimum needs at reassessment, or authorization is reduced or ended, the RN Director gets the written notice from the plan or district, informs the patient, helps the patient understand appeal and fair hearing rights as the notice states, and follows SVC-15 for any discharge or transition.

When the independent assessment was by telehealth, the intake coordinator confirms that the patient was offered an in-person option and notes it in the file. The agency does not require telehealth of a patient who prefers in-person.

For private-pay patients, no Medicaid documents are needed. The RN completes the professional assessment under SVC-05 and the acceptance determination under SVC-02, and the order requirement of SVC-07 applies.

The intake coordinator keeps every Medicaid eligibility document, authorization and plan notification in the clinical record and flags expiry dates. Billing staff verify authorization before each billing cycle (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Records payer information, requests and tracks Medicaid documents and authorizations, and flags expirations.
Review independent assessment and minimum needs, confirm level and authorized hours, complete the agency's assessment and plan, and notify plans or districts of changes.
Schedule only authorized hours and tasks.
Bill only authorized services and verify authorization before billing.
Ensures that no service starts without the required documents and that staff comply with minimum-needs and authorization rules.

documentation: Medicaid eligibility and payer information in the intake record
Independent RN assessment, independent medical exam and practitioner order
Plan or district authorization stating level, amount, frequency and duration
RN minimum-needs review note
Agency professional assessment and plan of care
Notifications to and from the plan or district about changes, reassessments and denials
Telehealth/in-person option documentation
Authorization expiry tracking log

policies.title: Nursing Services (RN Responsibilities and Standards of Practice)
policies.applies_to: RN Director, staff registered nurses, and all staff who receive nursing direction
policies.purpose: To define the nursing services [AGENCY NAME] provides, who provides them, and the professional standards they must meet, so that every patient's care is directed and supervised by a registered nurse as required by 10 NYCRR §766.9(h).
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet nursing items WS-NUR.1, WS-NUR.2, WS-NUR.3, WS-NUR.4, WS-NUR.5, WS-NUR.10, WS-NUR.11, WS-NUR.12, WS-NUR.13 and WS-NUR.14.

WS-NUR.1 — Responsibilities of nursing staff consistent with nursing practice standards. [AGENCY NAME] provides nursing services only through registered nurses. Each RN practices within the New York State Nurse Practice Act and the standards of the profession. The RN responsibilities are: accepting patients only after determining the agency can safely and adequately meet their needs (10 NYCRR §766.3(a)); performing the assessment and building the plan of care (§766.3(b)); teaching the patient and caregiver; supervising aides; coordinating care; documenting; and planning discharge. The RN Director directs and supervises all patient care (§766.9(h)).

WS-NUR.2 — Need for physician's orders. No nursing service is started without an order from the patient's authorized practitioner. Procedures for obtaining and maintaining orders are in SVC-07.

WS-NUR.3 — Who provides nursing services. Nursing services are provided by the RN Director, [RN DIRECTOR NAME], and by staff RNs employed by or contracted to [AGENCY NAME]. Every RN must hold a current license and registration to practice in New York State. A nurse practicing outside the scope of that license is not permitted to provide services.

WS-NUR.4 — Reference: scope of practice. RNs may perform only those functions within the scope of RN practice under the NYS Nurse Practice Act and State Education Department rules. An RN may not delegate a task to an aide that is outside the aide's permitted duties (see SVC-01).

WS-NUR.5 — Reference: standards of practice. RNs follow accepted standards of nursing practice, including the nursing process (assess, plan, implement, evaluate), accurate and timely documentation, patient safety, and infection control (SAF-03). The agency adds no nursing or therapeutic service until it has been reviewed by the QI committee (§766.2(a)(7)).

WS-NUR.10 — Coordination of services. The RN coordinates with the authorized practitioner, the MLTC plan care manager, and other providers serving the patient, and records each contact.

WS-NUR.11 — Clinical conferencing. The RN Director holds clinical case conferences at least monthly and whenever a patient's condition changes significantly. Conferences are documented.

WS-NUR.12 — Clinical documentation. The RN writes a signed and dated progress note after each visit or phone contact (§766.6(a)).

WS-NUR.13 — The plan of care. The RN builds the plan of care on the RN's own assessment and reviews it as described in SVC-06 (§766.3(b), (d)).

WS-NUR.14 — Discharge planning. The RN begins discharge planning before discharge (§766.2(a)(8)). Discharge occurs only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (§766.2(a)(9)). See SVC-15.

Supervision of aides (WS-NUR.9) is addressed in SVC-09 and SVC-10.

definitions.definition: The physician, doctor of osteopathy, podiatrist, licensed midwife or nurse practitioner who orders the patient's services.
The licensed, registered nurse the governing authority employs to direct and supervise all patient care.
A documented meeting at which the RN and other staff review a patient's condition, plan and progress.
A signed and dated entry written after each visit or telephone contact.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], verifies each RN's NYS license and current registration before hire and keeps the verification in the personnel file (see PER-08).

Before any patient is accepted, an RN, or a person directly supervised by an RN, determines whether the agency can safely and adequately meet the patient's needs, and documents the determination (§766.3(a); see SVC-02).
The RN confirms that a current order from the authorized practitioner is on file before the first nursing service is delivered (see SVC-07).
The RN completes the initial assessment before services start (see SVC-05).
The RN builds the plan of care from the assessment and sends it to the practitioner for review (see SVC-06).
The RN prepares the aide care plan and orients the assigned aide before the first visit (see SVC-08).
The RN delivers nursing services only within the RN scope of practice and the written plan of care. Any task outside that scope is referred to the practitioner or another appropriate provider.
After each visit or phone contact, the RN writes a signed and dated progress note in the clinical record (same day if possible, and no later than [24 HOURS] after the contact).
The RN contacts the authorized practitioner promptly about any significant change in condition and records the call, who was spoken to, and any new order (§766.3(d)(2)).
For MLTC enrollees, the RN contacts the plan care manager about changes in condition, new needs or service problems, and records the contact.
The RN coordinates with other providers involved in the patient's care (home health agency, therapy, adult day care, DME vendor) and notifies them of significant changes.

The RN Director holds a clinical conference at least monthly, and sooner when needed, to review new admissions, patients with changes in condition, incidents, and patients due for discharge. The RN Director records attendees, patients discussed and actions in the conference record.
The RN Director brings any proposed new nursing or therapeutic service to the QI committee before it is offered (§766.2(a)(7); see GOV-04).

The RN starts discharge planning before discharge, notifies the practitioner at least 48 hours before discharge, consults the patient and staff, and writes a discharge summary (§766.2(a)(8)-(9); see SVC-15).
The RN Director reviews a sample of RN progress notes each quarter for timeliness and completeness and reports findings to the QI committee.

responsibilities.duty: Employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care and provides enough staff (§766.9(g)-(h)).
Directs and supervises all patient care, assigns RNs by training and skill, leads clinical conferences, and reports to the QI committee.
Assesses, plans, delivers and documents nursing care within scope of practice and coordinates with the practitioner, plan and other providers.
Verifies RN licensure and registration and supplies the staff and resources needed for nursing services.

documentation: RN license and registration verification (personnel file)
Acceptance determination
Practitioner order
Signed and dated progress notes
Records of calls to the practitioner, MLTC care manager and other providers
Clinical conference records
Plan of care and plan reviews
Discharge summary
QI committee minutes on nursing services

policies.title: RN Assessment, Reassessment, Patient/Caregiver Education and Medications and Treatments
policies.applies_to: RN Director, staff registered nurses
policies.purpose: To make sure every patient receives a professional RN assessment before services start, is reassessed on a regular schedule and whenever the condition changes, receives documented teaching, and has medications and treatments accurately recorded in the plan of care.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet items WS-NUR.6, WS-NUR.7 and WS-NUR.8.

WS-NUR.6 — Assessments (initial, reassessment). An RN completes the initial assessment before services start. The plan of care is based on that professional assessment (10 NYCRR §766.3(b)). The RN reassesses at least every six months, matching the plan review required by §766.3(d)(1), and also whenever the patient's condition changes. Each assessment is documented in the clinical record (10 NYCRR §766.6(a)).

WS-NUR.7 — Patient/caregiver education. The RN teaches the patient and caregiver what they need to know about the plan of care, the patient's condition, safe practices, the role of the aide, the patient's rights and responsibilities, and when and how to contact the agency. The RN documents the teaching and how well it was understood.

WS-NUR.8 — Medications and treatments. The RN records all medications and treatments in the plan of care and reconciles them at each assessment. Aides may prompt or assist with medications as allowed for Level II personal care, but may not administer them (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(5)(ii)(a)(10); see SVC-11).

For Medicaid clients, an independent assessment and practitioner order are also required each year under 18 NYCRR §505.14(b). The independent assessment is done by the independent assessor, not by [AGENCY NAME]. It does not replace the agency's own RN assessment.

definitions.definition: The RN's in-person evaluation of the patient's health, functional abilities, home environment, supports and needs, completed before services start.
A repeat RN evaluation done at least every six months and whenever the condition changes.
Comparing the patient's current medication list against the plan of care, orders and pharmacy or practitioner records to find and resolve differences.
The annual assessment required for Medicaid personal care that is performed by an independent RN and independent medical examiner, separate from the agency's assessment (18 NYCRR §505.14(b)).

procedures: On referral, the RN Director assigns an RN to complete the initial assessment before any service begins.
The RN schedules the in-home assessment with the patient and, with the patient's permission, the caregiver and family.

The RN assesses diagnoses and history, prognosis, mental and emotional status, functional limitations, rehabilitation potential, diet, the home environment and safety, informal supports, and any need for palliative care.
The RN records current medications (name, dose, route, frequency, prescriber), allergies, and treatments. The RN compares them with the practitioner order and any list from the MLTC plan.
The RN resolves any difference in medications by contacting the authorized practitioner before finalizing the plan of care and records the result.
The RN records the initial assessment in the clinical record, signed and dated, and uses it to build the plan of care (see SVC-06).

For Medicaid clients, the RN checks that the independent assessment and practitioner order have been received and that they are consistent with the plan of care (see SVC-03 and SVC-17). The RN tracks the annual due date of the next independent assessment and practitioner order.
The RN reassesses each patient at least every six months. The RN Director keeps a due-date tracking list and reviews it each week.
The RN reassesses sooner after any significant change in condition, hospitalization, fall, new diagnosis, medication change, or an aide or family report of a new problem.
At each reassessment, the RN reconciles medications and treatments again, updates the plan of care, and notifies the practitioner of any significant change.
The RN teaches the patient and caregiver about the plan of care, the aide's duties and limits, safety, infection prevention, and how to reach the agency 24 hours a day at [PHONE].
The RN uses teach-back where appropriate, provides teaching in the patient's preferred language (see CR-06), and documents what was taught, who was taught, and the response.
The RN documents each assessment, medication reconciliation and teaching session in the clinical record by the end of the next business day.
The RN Director audits a sample of assessments each quarter for completeness, timeliness and reconciliation, and reports results to the QI committee.

responsibilities.duty: Completes initial assessments and reassessments, reconciles medications, teaches the patient and caregiver, and documents all three.
Assigns assessments, keeps the reassessment due-date list, and audits compliance.
Alert the RN Director to referrals and Medicaid assessment and order deadlines.
Provide accurate health and medication information and report changes.

documentation: Initial assessment form, signed and dated
Reassessment forms
Medication and treatment list with reconciliation notes
Teaching record
Practitioner contact notes
Medicaid independent assessment and practitioner order
Reassessment tracking list
QI audit results

policies.title: Plan of Care and Plan Updates
policies.applies_to: RN Director, staff registered nurses, intake staff
policies.purpose: To ensure that every patient has a written plan of care built on the RN's assessment, that it is kept current, and that all care is delivered under it.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet Plan of Care items WS-POC.1 through WS-POC.16.

The plan of care is:
- WS-POC.1: based on the RN's initial assessment (10 NYCRR §766.3(b)).
- WS-POC.2: established for each patient, with no exceptions.
- WS-POC.3: based on the patient's assessed and identified needs.
- WS-POC.4: reviewed and revised as frequently as necessary to reflect changes in the patient's condition (§766.3(d)(1); §766.5(b)).
- WS-POC.5: reviewed and revised at least every six months.
- WS-POC.6: documented in the clinical record with each review (§766.3(d)(1); §766.6(a)).

The plan of care must include:
- WS-POC.7: a pertinent diagnosis and prognosis.
- WS-POC.8: any identified need for palliative care (see SVC-16).
- WS-POC.9: the patient's mental and emotional status.
- WS-POC.10: the frequency of each service to be provided.
- WS-POC.11: medications.
- WS-POC.12: treatments.
- WS-POC.13: diet regimens.
- WS-POC.14: functional limitations and rehabilitation potential.
- WS-POC.15: orders for therapy services, including specific procedures and modalities, if needed (if the agency does not provide therapy, the plan records any therapy ordered and provided by others and notes the coordination).
- WS-POC.16: the frequency and duration of all services ordered.

For MLTC enrollees, the plan of care records the level, amount, frequency and duration of services authorized by the MLTC plan. The plan remains responsible for authorizing services and gives the enrollee notice (DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance). The agency does not deliver more or fewer hours than authorized without a revised authorization. Staff promptly alert the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in condition (§766.3(d)(2)).

definitions.definition: The patient's written plan, built on the RN's assessment, that states what services will be delivered, how often and for how long.
For Medicaid and MLTC patients, the level, amount, frequency and duration of services approved by the plan or district.
A change in health, function, cognition, safety or supports that may require a change in the plan, orders or services.

procedures: The assigned RN completes the initial assessment and uses it, not the referral form alone, to draft the plan of care before services start (see SVC-05).
The RN enters the pertinent diagnosis and prognosis from the assessment and the practitioner order.
The RN records whether the patient has a palliative care need or a life-limiting illness, and if so, links the plan to SVC-16.
The RN records the patient's mental and emotional status, including cognition, mood, and ability to direct their own care.
The RN lists the services to be delivered, the frequency of each, and the duration of each service ordered, including any therapy orders with procedures and modalities.
The RN enters medications, treatments, diet regimen, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential.

For an MLTC enrollee, the RN enters the level, amount, frequency and duration authorized by the plan and attaches or references the authorization notice. If the services do not match the authorization, the RN contacts the plan care manager before services start (see SVC-17).
The RN signs and dates the plan and sends it to the authorized practitioner for review and signature (see SVC-07). The RN files it in the clinical record.
The RN gives the patient (or representative) a copy or explains the plan, and documents this.
The RN writes the aide care plan from the plan of care and orients the aide before the first visit (see SVC-08).
The RN reviews and revises the plan whenever the condition changes and at least every six months. The RN Director's tracking list shows each patient's next review date.
At each review, the RN records the review in the clinical record with the date, findings, whether the plan was changed, and the RN's signature.

When a significant change occurs, the RN promptly alerts the authorized practitioner and other affected providers (and the plan care manager for MLTC enrollees) and records the date, time, person contacted, and any new orders (§766.3(d)(2)).
When a plan revision changes the aide's tasks or hours, the RN updates the aide care plan and notifies the aide before the next visit.
The RN Director audits plans of care each quarter for all required elements and timely six-month reviews, and reports results to the QI committee.

responsibilities.duty: Develops, reviews, revises and documents the plan of care and notifies the practitioner and affected providers of changes.
Ensures every patient has a plan, tracks six-month reviews and audits plans.
Reviews the plan and provides and authenticates orders.
Obtain MLTC authorizations and notify the RN of authorization changes.
Provides care under the aide care plan and reports changes; may not change the plan.

documentation: Plan of care, signed and dated by the RN
Six-month review entries
Interim revisions with reasons
MLTC or district authorization notices
Practitioner contact notes
Aide care plan
Review due-date tracking list
QI audit results

policies.title: Medical Orders
policies.applies_to: RN Director, staff registered nurses, intake and records staff
policies.purpose: To make sure that services are delivered only under a current order from an authorized practitioner, that orders are kept current and authenticated, and that verbal orders are handled safely.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet Medical Orders items WS-MO.1 through WS-MO.10.

WS-MO.1 — An order from the patient's authorized practitioner is obtained for all patients. No service starts without one.

WS-MO.2 — An authorized practitioner is a medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, doctor of podiatry, licensed midwife or nurse practitioner. The RN Director confirms this policy against the current text of the New York medical orders regulation (10 NYCRR Part 766) at each annual policy review.

WS-MO.3 — Orders are reviewed and revised as the patient's needs change.

WS-MO.4 — Orders are reviewed and revised at a minimum every six months, together with the plan of care (10 NYCRR §766.3(d)(1)).

WS-MO.5 — All orders reference all diagnoses, medications, treatments, prognoses, any need for palliative care, and any other information relevant to the patient's plan of care.

WS-MO.6 — All orders are authenticated by the authorized practitioner within 12 months.

WS-MO.7 — Changes in medical orders, including telephone orders, are authenticated by the authorized practitioner within 12 months.

WS-MO.8 — How orders are obtained: through written requests to the practitioner at referral and at each review, through the practitioner order for Medicaid personal care under 18 NYCRR §505.14(b), and through verbal orders taken as described below.

WS-MO.9 — Discharge planning: discharge planning begins before discharge (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(8)). Discharge occurs only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (§766.2(a)(9)). See SVC-15.

WS-MO.10 — Verbal orders are taken only by an RN, read back to the practitioner, written down, and signed by the RN.

definitions.definition: A medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, doctor of podiatry, licensed midwife or nurse practitioner who is responsible for the patient's care.
The practitioner's signature and date on an order or order change.
An order given by the practitioner by phone or in person that is not yet in writing.
Repeating the order word for word to the practitioner to confirm it was heard and written correctly.

procedures: At referral, intake staff identify the patient's authorized practitioner and give the name and contact details to the RN.

The RN requests a written order before the first service. For Medicaid personal care, the RN confirms that the practitioner order obtained under 18 NYCRR §505.14(b) is on file (see SVC-03 and SVC-17).

The RN checks that the order references the diagnoses, medications, treatments, prognosis, any palliative care need, and other pertinent information in the plan of care. If any element is missing, the RN requests clarification before services start.
The RN confirms from the practitioner's credentials that the signer is an MD, DO, podiatrist, licensed midwife or nurse practitioner. Orders from anyone else are not accepted.
The RN files the order in the clinical record and records the date received.

The RN reviews each patient's orders when the plan of care changes and at least every six months. The RN sends the updated plan to the practitioner for new or renewed orders. The tracking list shows each due date.
Only an RN may take a verbal order. Aides, office staff and other non-RN staff must not take orders and must transfer the call to the RN.
The RN writes the verbal order on the order form while the practitioner is speaking, reads it back, receives confirmation, then signs and dates it, recording the practitioner's name and the time.
The RN carries out the order and updates the plan of care and the aide care plan if the order changes aide tasks.
Within [7] days of taking a verbal order, the RN sends it to the practitioner for authentication. Records staff log the date sent.

Records staff track every unsigned order. If an order has not been authenticated after 30 days, the RN follows up with the practitioner and records the follow-up. No order may remain unauthenticated beyond 12 months.
The RN Director reports orders still unsigned at 12 months to the QI committee.

When discharge is planned, the RN starts discharge planning before discharge, notifies the practitioner at least 48 hours before discharge, consults the patient and staff, and records the notice (§766.2(a)(8)-(9)).
The RN Director audits orders each quarter for presence, completeness, authentication and verbal order handling, and reports to the QI committee.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains and reviews orders, takes and reads back verbal orders, follows up on authentication and notifies the practitioner of discharge.
Maintains the tracking of orders, audits compliance and confirms this policy against the regulation at annual review.
File orders, log dates sent and returned and flag overdue authentications.
Do not take orders and transfer the practitioner to an RN.
Provides, reviews and authenticates orders.

documentation: Practitioner orders for each patient
Medicaid practitioner order (for Medicaid clients)
Verbal order forms with read-back, signature and time
Order tracking log (sent, returned, follow-up)
Discharge notice to practitioner
QI audit results

policies.title: Aide Care Plan, Orientation to the Care Plan, Communication of Changes and Task Documentation
policies.applies_to: Registered nurses, personal care aides, scheduling staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every aide knows exactly which tasks to perform for each patient, is oriented to the plan before providing care, reports changes in condition immediately, and documents each visit.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet items WS-PCA.5, WS-PCA.6, WS-PCA.7 and WS-PCA.8.

WS-PCA.6 — The aide care plan. For each patient served by an aide, the RN prepares a written aide care plan from the plan of care. It lists the specific tasks the aide is to perform, the frequency and times, special precautions, diet, what to observe and report, and who to call.

WS-PCA.5 — Orientation to the care plan. Before the aide's first visit, the RN orients the aide to the patient and the aide care plan. If the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, the RN is present at the initial service visit and has the aide demonstrate the tasks (10 NYCRR §766.5(d)(1)). The same applies when a change in personnel occurs.

WS-PCA.7 — Communication process for changes in patient condition. Aides report any change in condition, adverse reaction, or problem with informal supports or the home to the RN right away (§766.5(b)). The RN follows up, notifies the authorized practitioner as required (§766.3(d)(2)), and revises the plan as needed. Aides may never change the care plan.

WS-PCA.8 — Documentation of tasks. The aide records each task on the aide activity sheet at every visit. The activity sheets are kept in the clinical record (10 NYCRR §766.6(a)).

definitions.definition: A written task list for the aide taken from the plan of care.
The record on which the aide documents the tasks performed and observations made at each visit.
Any new or worsening symptom, injury, behavior, adverse reaction, or problem with the home or informal supports.
The aide performs a task while the RN watches to confirm competence.

procedures: After the plan of care is complete, the RN writes the aide care plan in plain language, listing each task, frequency, times, precautions, diet, and observations to report. The aide care plan must be consistent with the authorized hours and tasks.
The RN Director reviews the aide care plan for tasks outside aide scope (see SVC-01) before it is released.
Scheduling staff assign aides according to their training and demonstrated skill and the RN's directions (see SVC-12).
Before the first visit, the RN meets or speaks with the assigned aide, reviews the aide care plan task by task, and explains the patient's condition, precautions, and emergency steps.

If the aide lacks documented training and experience in any task, or when a different aide is assigned, the RN goes to the initial visit, directs the aide, and obtains a return demonstration (§766.5(d)(1)).
The aide receives a copy of the aide care plan, which is kept in the home, and signs that orientation was received. The RN records the orientation in the clinical record.

At every visit, the aide completes the aide activity sheet, checking off or noting each task performed, any task not performed and why, and relevant observations. The aide signs and dates it. For visits recorded through EVV, tasks are still documented on the sheet (see SVC-13).
Aides return completed activity sheets to the office [WEEKLY] and records staff file them in the clinical record.

The aide reports immediately to the RN at [PHONE] any change in condition, adverse reaction, injury, refusal of care, or problem with informal supports or the home. In an emergency, the aide calls 911 first, then the RN (see SVC-14).
The RN records each report, assesses the patient (by phone or visit as needed), notifies the practitioner promptly of any significant change, and revises the plan and aide care plan as needed.
The RN gives the aide any revised aide care plan and instructions before the next visit and documents that the aide understood.
The aide must not add, remove or change a task. If asked by the patient or family to do so, the aide declines politely and tells the RN.
The RN reviews activity sheets at each supervisory visit and at least monthly, and follows up on gaps or unmet tasks.

responsibilities.duty: Writes the aide care plan, orients the aide, follows up on reported changes and revises the plan.
Reviews aide care plans for scope and audits orientation and activity sheet documentation.
Follows the aide care plan exactly, documents each visit, and reports changes immediately.
Assign aides appropriately and collect activity sheets.
File activity sheets in the clinical record.

documentation: Aide care plan
Aide orientation record with RN and aide signatures
Return demonstration record (when applicable)
Aide activity sheets
Record of reports of changes in condition and RN follow-up
Revised aide care plans with date of notice to aide

policies.title: Clinical Supervision of All Services and Paraprofessional Staff
policies.applies_to: Governing authority, RN Director, supervising RNs, personal care aides and all clinical staff
policies.purpose: To ensure that all services and all paraprofessional staff are supervised so that care is delivered safely, according to the plan of care, and by suitably trained staff.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Applicant Worksheet Clinical Supervision items WS-CS.1 through WS-CS.8 and nursing item WS-NUR.9.

WS-CS.1 — Supervision of all services. All services the agency provides are supervised by the RN Director or a supervising RN, who directs and oversees all patient care (10 NYCRR §766.9(h)). Supervision includes case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation, and consultation on policy (10 NYCRR §766.5(b)).

WS-CS.2 and WS-NUR.9 — Supervision of paraprofessional staff and aides. Aides are supervised as appropriate by an RN (§766.5(c)). Details of RN in-home supervisory visits are in SVC-10.

WS-CS.3 — Sufficient supervisory staff. The governing authority ensures there are enough trained supervisory staff to provide quality care (§766.5(a)).

WS-CS.4 — Routine supervision. Staff are routinely supervised to ensure care is provided according to the plan of care.

WS-CS.5 — In-home visits and frequency. Supervision includes in-home visits. An RN visits in the home: at the initial service visit or on a change in personnel, if the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, with return demonstration; when a change in condition occurs, to evaluate and revise the plan; and to instruct the aide on required observations and written reports (§766.5(d)). The routine frequency of supervisory visits is set in SVC-10 and is never less often than these requirements. If the agency ever employs advanced home health aides, an RN must visit at least every two weeks (§766.5(e)); the agency does not currently use them.

WS-CS.6 — Assignment of staff. All staff are assigned according to their licensure, discipline, training, orientation and demonstrated skills.

WS-CS.7 — Plans of care are revised as needed (§766.3(d); §766.5(b)).

WS-CS.8 — Clinical consultation, orientation and training. The RN Director provides clinical consultation, orientation and training for staff.

definitions.definition: Case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation and consultation on policy.
Personal care aides and other unlicensed caregivers who deliver care under RN direction.
An RN visit in the patient's home to direct and evaluate the aide's care.
Competence shown through documented training, competency evaluation and observed performance.

procedures: The governing authority determines the number of supervising RNs needed based on the active patient census, number of aides, geographic spread and acuity, and reviews this at least quarterly. The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], documents the decision.
The RN Director, [RN DIRECTOR NAME], assigns each patient to a supervising RN responsible for that patient's case review.

Scheduling staff assign each aide by licensure, training, orientation and demonstrated skill, using the competency record kept under PER-05. An aide is not assigned to a task or patient for which competence has not been documented.
The supervising RN reviews each case at the clinical conferences described in SVC-04 and on any change in condition, and documents the review.

The supervising RN makes in-home supervisory visits as follows: at the initial service visit or on a change in aide, if the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, with return demonstration; on a change in condition, to evaluate the patient and revise the plan; and to instruct the aide on required observations and written reports (§766.5(d)). Routine visits follow SVC-10.
At each visit, the RN observes care, compares it with the plan of care and aide care plan, checks the activity sheets, and talks with the patient about their satisfaction.
The RN records each supervisory visit in a supervisory report in the clinical record, including findings, instructions given, and follow-up (§766.6(a)).
The RN Director checks monthly that services were delivered at the planned times and frequencies, using schedules, activity sheets and EVV data (see SVC-12 and SVC-13).

The supervising RN confirms that changes in condition, adverse reactions, and problems with informal supports or the home were charted and reported promptly, and revises the plan of care when needed (§766.5(b)).
When an aide does not follow the care plan, the RN corrects the aide on the spot, documents it, retrains the aide, and refers repeated problems to the Administrator under PER-10.

The RN Director provides clinical consultation to staff on request and holds orientation and training for new clinical and aide staff (see PER-05). Consultation on policy is available through the RN Director and the Administrator.
Aides are told how to reach the RN [24 HOURS A DAY] at [PHONE] for clinical questions.
The RN Director reports supervision results (visit completion, missed or late visits, corrective actions) to the QI committee each quarter (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures sufficient trained supervisory staff (§766.5(a)) and supports the RN Director's authority.
Directs and supervises all patient care, assigns supervising RNs, monitors supervision and provides clinical consultation and training.
Performs case review and in-home visits, documents supervisory reports and revises plans.
Assign aides by training and demonstrated skill.
Accept direction, follow plans and report changes.

documentation: Supervisory staffing review
Supervisory visit reports
Return demonstration records
Clinical conference records
Aide competency records
Corrective action and retraining records
Schedules, activity sheets and EVV reports reviewed
QI committee reports on supervision

policies.title: RN In-Home Supervisory Visits of Aides
policies.applies_to: All registered nurses, supervisors, schedulers and personal care aides of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every aide is directed, taught and evaluated in the patient's home by a registered nurse (RN). Care is then delivered safely, at the planned times and frequencies, and according to the plan of care. Supervision is recorded in writing for the clinical record and for state and payer review.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides clinical supervision of all aides through in-home visits by an RN supervisor, as required by 10 NYCRR §766.5 and, for Medicaid personal care, 18 NYCRR §505.14(f). This policy addresses the following Applicant Worksheet p.7 items (RN Supervision policy/procedure) and p.2 item:

• WS-RNS.1 (initial aide visit): The RN supervisor conducts an in-home visit at the initial aide service visit for each new patient. The RN also conducts one when the aide changes and the new aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks to be performed (10 NYCRR §766.5(d)(1)).
• WS-RNS.2 (demonstrate and instruct): At that visit the RN demonstrates to and instructs the aide in the treatments and services to be provided. The aide gives a return demonstration.
• WS-RNS.3 (every 6 months): The RN supervisor conducts in-home visits at least every 6 months for every patient receiving aide services.
• WS-RNS.4 (change in condition, needs or environment): The RN supervisor conducts an in-home visit whenever the patient's condition, needs or environment change (§766.5(d)(2)), to evaluate the change and revise the plan of care.
• WS-RNS.5 (instruct and review written reports): The RN instructs the aide on the observations to make and the written reports to complete, and reviews those reports (§766.5(d)(3)).
• WS-RNS.6 (recorded in writing): Every supervisory visit is recorded in a written report, filed in the clinical record (10 NYCRR §766.6(a)).
• WS-PCA.4 (who supervises the PCA, and how often): Each aide is supervised by the RN assigned to the patient's case. This is the RN Director, [RN DIRECTOR NAME], or a designated agency RN supervisor. Frequency is at least every 6 months for all patients and on any change as above. For Medicaid personal care it is at least every 90 days, unless the local district or MLTC plan has set a different frequency in writing (18 NYCRR §505.14(f)). The applicable frequency is stated on each patient's plan of care.

The agency uses the 90-day interval for Medicaid patients as its operating standard. OMIG audit guidance (not a legal requirement) describes disallowance of claims where no RN supervisory visit occurred within 120 days before the date of service. The agency therefore schedules visits early enough to stay inside that window.

definitions.definition: An in-home visit by an RN with the aide present, to direct and evaluate care, instruct the aide, and review the patient's condition, home environment and the aide's written reports.
The aide performs a task while the RN observes, to show the aide can do it correctly and safely.
Assignment of a different aide to a patient, including a permanent replacement or a new regular substitute.
The Medicaid managed long term care plan or other Medicaid managed care organization that authorizes the patient's services.

procedures: At acceptance, the RN Director assigns each patient a supervising RN. The RN records the name of that RN and the required supervisory visit frequency on the plan of care and the aide care plan (see SVC-06 and SVC-08).

For Medicaid patients, the RN checks the MLTC plan contract or district authorization for any stated supervision frequency. If none is stated, the 90-day standard applies. The RN records the frequency and its source on the plan of care. The RN Director confirms the current text of 18 NYCRR §505.14(f) and each plan contract at least annually.

Before the first aide visit, the RN reviews the assigned aide's documented training, certification and experience (PER-02) against the tasks on the aide care plan. The RN notes any task for which training or experience is not documented.

The RN attends the initial aide service visit in the patient's home. If the aide is later replaced and the new aide lacks documented training and experience in the assigned tasks, the RN attends the first visit by the new aide.

At that visit the RN reviews the aide care plan with the aide and the patient. The RN demonstrates each task not previously documented, and the aide gives a return demonstration. The RN repeats instruction until the aide performs the task correctly and safely.

If an aide cannot perform a task safely after instruction, the RN does not permit the aide to perform it unsupervised. The RN notifies the RN Director, who arranges retraining or reassignment and documents the action.

The RN instructs the aide on what to observe (condition changes, skin, intake, mood, falls, medication issues, safety hazards, problems with family or other supports). The RN also instructs the aide on what to report to the RN and how to complete the aide activity sheet (SVC-08).

The scheduler keeps a supervision tracker with the last visit date and next due date for every patient. Each week the tracker is reviewed by the RN Director. Visits that will fall due within 14 days are assigned to an RN. A visit due within 15 days is escalated to the RN Director.

The RN makes routine visits at the set frequency, at least every 6 months for all patients. The target for Medicaid patients is every 90 days, scheduled so the visit occurs well inside 120 days of any date of service.

The RN makes an additional in-home visit when an aide, patient, family member or other provider reports a change in condition, needs or environment. The visit occurs within 2 business days of the report, or sooner if clinically indicated. At it the RN evaluates the change and revises the plan of care (SVC-06, SVC-14).
The aide must be present for the visit. A visit made without the aide present is documented but does not count as the supervisory visit. The scheduler arranges a replacement visit.

During the visit the RN observes the aide performing tasks. The RN also reviews the aide's written reports and activity sheets, checks aide attendance against the schedule, and confirms the aide carries current agency ID. The RN assesses the patient's condition and satisfaction, home safety, and the adequacy of informal supports.

The RN completes a written supervisory visit report. It records the date and times, who was present, tasks observed, return demonstrations, instruction given, findings, changes needed to the plan, and follow-up. The RN signs and dates it. It is completed within 2 business days of the visit and filed in the clinical record.

If the visit finds that the plan or aide care plan needs revision, the RN revises it and notifies the aide of the change. The RN notifies the authorized practitioner and MLTC plan or district when required (SVC-07, SVC-17).

The RN Director reviews reports with performance concerns. Corrective action may include retraining, competency re-evaluation, closer supervision or reassignment, and is documented in the personnel record (PER-08).

The RN Director reports timeliness of supervisory visits (on time, late, missed) to the QI Committee at each meeting (GOV-04). Any visit overdue by more than 30 days is a quality-of-care concern and is reviewed by the Administrator.

The agency does not currently employ advanced home health aides. If the license is amended to add them, this policy will be revised before they are used to add the RN home visit at least every two weeks required by §766.5(e).

responsibilities.duty: Assigns supervising RNs; monitors the supervision tracker; reviews reports; ensures visits meet the required frequency; confirms current payer and regulatory frequency requirements.
Conducts initial, routine and event-triggered in-home visits; demonstrates and instructs; reviews written reports; completes and files the visit report; revises the plan of care.
Maintains the tracker; schedules aide presence for visits; alerts the RN Director to due and overdue visits.
Is present for supervisory visits; performs return demonstrations; follows RN instruction; completes and submits written observations and activity sheets; reports changes.
Provides enough supervisory staff (§766.5(a)) and reviews overdue visits.

documentation: Written supervisory visit report for each visit, signed and dated by the RN
Return demonstration and instruction record
Supervision tracker with due and completed dates
Supervision frequency and its source noted on the plan of care
Revised plan of care and aide care plan, when changed
Corrective action records, when applicable
QI Committee reports on supervisory visit timeliness

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
policies.applies_to: Registered nurses, Level II personal care aides and schedulers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define the limited help aides may give with medications a client takes by themselves. The policy protects clients from medication errors and keeps aides within their scope.
policies.policy: Under 18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(5)(ii)(a)(10), Level II personal care aides may prompt and assist clients with self-administered medication. They may not administer medication. [AGENCY NAME] limits aides to the assistance the RN has assessed as appropriate and listed in the plan of care and aide care plan. The RN documents each client's medications in the plan of care. Aides record every assistance and report missed doses, refusals and adverse reactions to the RN at once. Aides never inject medication, adjust doses, or set up or fill medication organizers beyond what the RN has assessed and the plan permits. Level I aides do not provide medication assistance.

definitions.definition: Reminding the client that it is time to take a medication that the client takes by themselves.
Physical help, within the limits set by the RN in the plan of care, so the client can take the client's own medication. The client remains the person who takes it.
Giving a medication to a client, deciding on or changing a dose, or injecting. This is not permitted for aides.
Personal care that includes personal care functions in addition to nutritional and environmental support tasks (18 NYCRR §505.14(a)(5)(ii)).

procedures: At assessment, the RN reviews the client's medications (name, dose, route, time, prescriber) and the client's ability to self-administer. The RN documents these in the plan of care (SVC-05, SVC-06).

The RN decides whether the client needs prompting or assistance and which exact actions are permitted. The RN writes those actions on the aide care plan (SVC-08). If a client cannot self-direct medication taking, the RN does not assign medication assistance and tells the client, the authorized practitioner and the payer so other arrangements can be made.

The RN verifies that the assigned aide is Level II and trained in medication prompting and assistance. The RN instructs the aide on the client's specific medications and permitted actions, with return demonstration where needed (SVC-10).

Aides assist only with medications listed on the current aide care plan, in the original labeled containers, at the times shown. The aide does not act on verbal instructions from family members, the client, or others to add, change or stop a medication. The aide reports such requests to the RN.
When the authorized practitioner changes a medication, the RN updates the plan of care and aide care plan, and tells the aide before the aide assists with the change (SVC-07).

The aide prompts and assists only as listed on the care plan. The aide never administers a medication, injects, adjusts a dose, crushes or splits a medication, or fills or sets up organizers beyond what the RN has assessed and the plan permits.
The aide records each assistance (date, time, medication reminded or assisted, and the client's response) on the activity sheet (SVC-08).

If a client refuses or misses a dose, the aide does not force or persuade the client against the client's wishes. The aide notifies the RN at once. The RN assesses the situation, contacts the authorized practitioner as needed, and documents the notification.

The aide reports any suspected adverse reaction, confusion, or wrong or unlabeled medication to the RN at once. In a life-threatening situation the aide calls 911 first, then notifies the RN (SVC-14).
A medication error or near-miss involving an aide is reported to the RN and documented on an incident report (SAF-02). The RN assesses the client, notifies the authorized practitioner, and documents.
At supervisory visits the RN reviews medication assistance records against the plan, observes the aide, and checks the client's understanding (SVC-10, §766.5(d)(3)).
The RN re-evaluates medication assistance needs at each reassessment and whenever the client's condition changes, and revises the plan (SVC-05).
The RN Director reviews medication events and trends quarterly for the QI Committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Assesses ability; documents medications and permitted aide actions; instructs and supervises aides; responds to reports of missed doses, refusals and reactions.
Prompts and assists only as listed; records each assistance; reports problems immediately; never administers.
Ensures only qualified aides are assigned; reviews events and trends.
Does not assign aides to medication-assistance tasks unless the RN has confirmed qualification.

documentation: Medication list and permitted aide actions in the plan of care
Aide care plan listing medication assistance tasks
Aide activity sheet entries for each assistance
RN notes on missed doses, refusals, reactions and practitioner notification
Incident reports for medication events
Supervisory visit reports

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
policies.applies_to: Schedulers, registered nurses, personal care aides and the RN Director of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure clients receive their authorized and planned services at the planned times and frequencies, with the same caregivers where possible. When visits are missed or late, coverage is arranged and the people responsible are told.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] schedules the same personnel to serve the same patient where possible (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(3)). Services are delivered at the planned times and frequencies (§766.5(b)). Aides are assigned by licensure, training and demonstrated skill. Every missed or late visit is logged. The scheduler arranges coverage and tells the RN and the client. Repeated missed visits are reported to the MLTC plan. Round-the-clock coverage and the emergency plan keep care going during disruptions (§766.9(c), (o)).

definitions.definition: A scheduled visit that does not occur, or in which the aide is not present for the scheduled time.
A visit starting later than [30] minutes after the scheduled start time unless the client agreed to the change.
Assigning the same regular aide, with a named back-up, to a patient so the patient receives consistent care.

procedures: At acceptance, the RN Director and scheduler review the plan of care and aide care plan for the days, hours and frequency of each service. The scheduler builds the schedule to match them.

The scheduler assigns a regular aide by licensure, training and demonstrated skill, and with the RN's review of the patient's needs. A named back-up aide who knows the client is also assigned where possible.

The scheduler tells the client the aide's name and schedule and gives the agency phone [PHONE] for questions and changes. Changes to the schedule are made only with the client's agreement and are noted in the record.

The scheduler changes the regular aide only for a good reason, such as an aide's leave, a client request, or a performance or safety concern. The RN is told of a change in personnel, because a supervisory visit may be needed (SVC-10).

An aide who will be late or unable to attend calls the scheduler at [PHONE] as early as possible and before the visit starts. The aide does not leave a client early or without arranging relief unless it is an emergency.
The scheduler records every missed or late visit in the missed-visit log with date, client, aide, reason, and action taken.
The scheduler immediately seeks coverage from the back-up aide, then other qualified aides. The scheduler calls the client to tell them of the delay and the arrangements.

If the scheduler cannot arrange coverage, the scheduler tells the RN at once. The RN assesses the risk to the client (such as need for help with toileting, meals or medications) and arranges other help, which may include contact with family or caregivers, or emergency services when a client may be unsafe.
The scheduler tells the RN of each missed visit the same day. The RN decides if the client needs a follow-up call or visit.

For Medicaid clients, the RN Director notifies the MLTC plan or local district when there are repeated missed visits (two or more in a 30-day period) or any pattern of missed visits. The notice is made within [3] business days after the second missed visit and recorded in the log.
When a client declines or is not home for a scheduled visit, the aide notifies the scheduler. The scheduler logs it and tells the RN if the pattern suggests a change in condition or need (SVC-14).
The agency maintains 24-hour, 7-day coverage by phone and RN on-call, so clients can reach the agency for scheduling problems and emergencies (10 NYCRR §766.9(f), (o); see GOV-07).
During an emergency or other disruption, the scheduler follows the Emergency Preparedness Plan and patient classification levels (SAF-05, SAF-06) to prioritize visits.
The RN Director reviews the log monthly. Trends such as missed visits per aide or per client and the number of aide changes are reported to the QI Committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Builds schedules from plans of care; assigns regular and back-up aides; logs and covers missed visits; notifies client and RN.
Assesses risk when coverage fails; follows up with clients; sees that changes in aides are supervised.
Arrives on time; calls promptly if late or absent; does not leave a client unsafe.
Notifies MLTC plans of repeated missed visits; reviews trends; provides report to QI Committee.
Ensures enough staff and on-call coverage.

documentation: Missed and late visit log
Schedules and assignment records showing regular and back-up aides
Notes of client and RN notifications
Notices to the MLTC plan or district
Monthly review and QI Committee reports

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
policies.applies_to: Personal care aides, schedulers, payroll and billing staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To verify electronically that Medicaid personal care visits occurred as authorized, and to keep accurate time and payment records.
policies.policy: Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) is required for Medicaid personal care services under the federal 21st Century Cures Act (42 USC 1396b(l)), effective in New York since 1/1/2021. New York uses the choice model: [AGENCY NAME] selects its own EVV vendor, and visit data is sent to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator. EVV captures the date, location, service, the people involved, and start and end times of each visit. EVV exceptions are resolved within the agency's set time, and the scheduler documents each manual edit with the reason. The agency keeps time and payment records (10 NYCRR §766.11(h)).

definitions.definition: Electronic Visit Verification: electronic capture of the date, location, service, the aide and client, and start and end times of a visit.
The New York State system that receives EVV data from provider EVV systems.
A visit record that is missing, incomplete or inconsistent with the schedule (for example a missed clock-in, location mismatch, or time outside the authorized schedule).
A change to an EVV record made by staff, rather than captured automatically.

procedures: The Administrator selects an EVV vendor that meets New York requirements and sends data to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator. The agency tests the data feed before billing Medicaid personal care and checks it regularly after that.
The scheduler enters each Medicaid personal care client, aide and authorized service into the EVV system so every scheduled visit matches the plan of care and authorization.
New aides are trained at orientation on how to clock in and out, what to do if the system does not work, and why accurate time records matter (PER-05).

The aide clocks in at the client's home at the start of the visit and clocks out at the end, using the method set by the vendor. The record captures date, location, service, aide and client, and start and end times.

The aide never clocks in or out for another person, outside of the client's location, or before arriving or after leaving. The aide does not share login credentials. Violations are handled under PER-10 and GOV-05.

If the system does not work, the aide calls the scheduler at [PHONE] from the client's home. The scheduler records the visit manually, with the reason, and the aide confirms the times on the activity sheet (SVC-08).
The scheduler reviews the exception report every business day. Each EVV exception is resolved within 3 business days of the visit by contacting the aide, client or RN as necessary.

Each manual edit is documented with the reason, the person who made it, the date and the supporting source (for example call to the aide). Manual edits are reviewed by the RN Director, or other supervisor, each week.
Billing staff bill Medicaid personal care only for visits that match the authorization and EVV record. Any mismatch is resolved or the claim is held (GOV-05).
Payroll uses the verified visit time records. Compensation, including overtime and any required wage parity, is paid as set out in PER-09.
The agency keeps time and payment records for each employee and retains them under REC-03 (§766.11(h)).
The Compliance Officer audits a sample of EVV records against schedules, activity sheets and payroll each quarter, and reports results to the QI Committee (GOV-04, GOV-05).
The agency keeps EVV data confidential and secure under CR-04.

responsibilities.duty: Selects and oversees the EVV vendor; ensures data reaches the Aggregator.
Loads schedules; reviews and resolves exceptions; documents manual edits.
Clocks in and out accurately at the client's home; reports system problems at once.
Bill and pay only on verified time; retain records.
Audits EVV records and reports to the QI Committee.

documentation: EVV visit records and Aggregator transmission confirmations
Exception reports and resolution notes
Manual edit log with reasons and approver
Aide activity sheets
Time and payment records
Quarterly EVV audit results

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
policies.applies_to: Registered nurses, personal care aides, schedulers and on-call staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure changes in a client's condition and emergencies are recognized, reported and acted on right away. The authorized practitioner and other affected providers are told promptly, and the plan of care is revised.
policies.policy:
Aides report any change in a client's condition to the RN right away. In a life-threatening emergency the aide calls 911 first. The RN promptly alerts the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in the patient's condition (10 NYCRR §766.3(d)(2)) and documents it. After a change, the RN makes an in-home visit to evaluate the client and revise the plan (§766.5(d)(2)). An incident report is completed when the event involves injury or harm (see SAF-02).

This policy meets Applicant Worksheet p.7 item WS-CR.16 — notification to the authorized practitioner of changes in patient condition.

definitions.definition: Any new or worsening sign, symptom, behavior, function or circumstance (for example fall, new confusion, pain, skin breakdown, poor intake, refusal of care, or an unsafe home).
The physician, nurse practitioner or other practitioner authorized by law to order the patient's care.
A situation that is an immediate threat to life or safety (for example chest pain, trouble breathing, unresponsiveness, stroke signs, severe bleeding, serious fall, fire).

procedures: In a life-threatening emergency the aide calls 911 first, gives the client's address and the nature of the emergency, and stays with the client, giving only the help the aide is trained to give. The aide does not diagnose or give treatment outside the aide's scope.
As soon as the emergency is under control, the aide calls the agency at [PHONE], and the RN or on-call RN is notified. Aides reach an RN 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

For any other change in condition, the aide calls the RN right away, and does not wait until the end of the shift or the next supervisory visit. The aide gives a clear description of what was observed and the client's current status.
The RN triages the report by phone, decides whether the client needs 911, urgent care, a call to the practitioner, or an RN visit, and tells the aide what to do.

The RN promptly notifies the authorized practitioner of any significant change. The RN documents the date and time, the name of the practitioner or office contacted, what was reported, the response, and any new orders (SVC-07).

The RN notifies the client's representative or family contact (with the client's permission), and tells other affected providers, such as the MLTC plan care manager, adult day program, or other agencies, of the change. For Medicaid clients the RN tells the MLTC plan or district when the change may affect services (SVC-17).

The RN makes an in-home visit to evaluate the client and revise the plan of care when a change in condition occurs. The visit occurs within 2 business days, or sooner if clinically indicated (SVC-10).
The RN revises the plan of care and the aide care plan as needed, and tells the aide of changes before the next visit (SVC-06, SVC-08). Where needed the RN does a reassessment (SVC-05).
If the client is taken to hospital, the RN confirms where, tells the practitioner and payer, and plans for return to service, with a reassessment before services resume.
If an event causes injury or harm, or involves abuse, neglect, or exploitation, the aide and RN complete the reports required under SAF-02 and SAF-01.
The RN documents the change, actions taken and follow-up in a dated and signed progress note in the clinical record (10 NYCRR §766.6(a)).
The RN calls the client or family the next day to check on the client's status after an emergency or serious change, and records the call.

The RN Director reviews emergencies and condition changes quarterly for patterns, such as falls, and reports to the QI Committee (GOV-04). Aides are retrained on recognition and reporting as needed (PER-05).

responsibilities.duty: Calls 911 for emergencies; reports any change to the RN immediately; documents observations; stays with client until help arrives where safe.
Triages reports; notifies the authorized practitioner and other providers promptly; visits the home; revises plans; documents.
Reviews emergencies and trends; ensures 24/7 RN access.
Routes aide calls to the RN at once and adjusts the schedule after a change.

documentation: RN progress notes of changes, practitioner notification (date, time, person, response) and orders
Aide reports and activity sheet entries
Revised plan of care and aide care plan
Incident report when injury or harm occurs
Notices to family, MLTC plan or district and other providers
Quarterly review for the QI Committee

policies.title: Discharge Planning, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
policies.applies_to: Registered nurses, RN Director, schedulers, billing staff and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every discharge, transfer or discontinuation of services is planned, safe, timely and appropriate. The authorized practitioner, the patient and the care team are involved, and the process is documented.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] begins discharge planning before discharge (10 NYCRR §766.2(a)(8)) and discharges a patient only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (§766.2(a)(9)). This policy meets the following Applicant Worksheet p.5 items (Discharge Planning policy/procedure):

• WS-DIS.1 — need to initiate discharge planning prior to discharge. The RN starts the plan before any discharge or transfer takes place, and the process starts at admission by identifying goals and expected end of service.
• WS-DIS.2 — need for a safe, timely and appropriate discharge or transfer. The RN makes sure the patient's needs after discharge are met or referred, with a discharge date that allows for safe arrangements.
• WS-DIS.3 — notification to the authorized practitioner at least 48 hours prior to discharge, documented in the clinical record.
• WS-DIS.4 — consultation with the patient/caregiver on the discharge plan.
• WS-DIS.5 — consultation with other professional staff on the discharge plan.

A discharge summary is written for the clinical record (§766.6(a)(10)). Patients are told of their right to complain, including to the Department of Health, and of any changes in charges, in line with 10 NYCRR §766.1.

definitions.definition: Ending of all services by [AGENCY NAME] for a patient, for any reason.
Movement of the patient's care to another agency, provider or level of care.
The RN's written plan for the patient's needs and arrangements after services end, including referrals and follow-up.
The physician or other practitioner authorized by law to order the patient's care.
A written summary in the clinical record of services provided, the patient's status at discharge, the reason for discharge and the plan after discharge.

procedures: At admission and at each plan of care review, the RN identifies the goals of care, expected length of services and any factors that could lead to discharge or transfer, such as goals met, no further need, a move, hospitalization, patient request, loss of authorization, or inability of the agency to meet the patient's needs safely (SVC-02, SVC-06).

When discharge or transfer is under consideration, the RN begins a written discharge plan before any date is set. The plan covers the patient's continuing needs, available supports, referrals and follow-up.

The RN consults the patient, or the patient's representative if the patient lacks capacity, and the caregiver, about the reasons for discharge, the plan and the date. The RN records the discussion and the patient's views.
The RN consults the aide, the scheduler and other professional staff involved, and other providers when needed, such as the MLTC plan care manager. The consultation is recorded.
The RN notifies the authorized practitioner of the planned discharge at least 48 hours before the discharge date. The RN records the date and time, the person notified and the response.

The discharge date is set so referrals and arrangements are in place and the patient is not left without needed care. Where a safe discharge cannot be arranged in that time, the RN Director and Administrator review the case before any date is final.

The RN gives the patient written notice of the discharge, the reason, the date and the arrangements for follow-up care. The notice includes the patient's right to complain without reprisal, including to the NYS Department of Health, and the agency's grievance process (CR-01, CR-03). The agency also gives any notice and appeal rights required by the patient's payer or the district.
For Medicaid clients, the RN Director notifies the MLTC plan or local district of the planned discharge or transfer, and coordinates so the plan can arrange other services without a gap (SVC-17).
The RN makes referrals and, with the patient's consent, sends needed information to the receiving provider, such as the plan of care, medication list and discharge summary, in line with CR-04.

If services end because of the patient's death, an unplanned hospital or facility admission, or an immediate safety threat, the RN notifies the authorized practitioner as soon as the agency learns of it. The circumstances and actions are documented.
On the discharge date the RN confirms services end, the schedule is cancelled, and agency property is collected from the home and the client's property is returned (CR-05).
The RN writes the discharge summary within [7] days of the discharge, and files it in the clinical record with notice to the practitioner, the discharge plan and consultation records (§766.6(a)(10)).
The scheduler and billing staff close the case in the scheduling, EVV and billing systems (SVC-13, GOV-05).
The agency keeps the record securely for at least 6 years after discharge, or longer for minors as required (REC-02). It is available to DOH.
The RN Director reviews discharges and transfers, including reasons and complaints, for the QI Committee each quarter (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Starts and documents the discharge plan; consults patient and staff; notifies the practitioner at least 48 hours ahead; writes the discharge summary.
Reviews difficult discharges; notifies MLTC plans or districts; ensures safe, timely transfer.
Approves discharges for reasons other than goals met or patient request, when needed; ensures notice to the patient.
Stop services and billing on the discharge date; support transfer.

documentation: Written discharge plan
Record of consultation with the patient/caregiver and with professional staff
Record of notice to the authorized practitioner (date, time, person)
Written notice to the patient
