The RN Director records the report, confirms the employee is safe, arranges coverage so the patient's needs are addressed (SVC-12), and assesses the patient's safety. If a patient is left without necessary care, the RN Director follows SVC-14.

The RN Director completes an incident report (SAF-02) for any threat, assault, injury, or serious unsafe condition, and notifies the Administrator within 24 hours. The Administrator ensures that any employee injury is reported as workers' compensation requires and that the employee is offered medical care and support.

After an incident, the RN Director or RN reassesses the home and the plan of care (SVC-06) and decides on changes: two-person visits, a different aide, changed hours, a supervised visit, or other measures. The RN also decides whether discharge under SVC-15 is warranted. These decisions and their reasons are recorded.
The RN Director conducts an in-home supervisory visit (SVC-10) when an aide reports a hazard or an unsafe pattern, and also uses that visit to observe the aide's safe handling technique.
The Administrator reviews all safety incidents with the QI Committee at least quarterly to identify trends and corrective action (GOV-04).
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually as part of the personnel policy review (10 NYCRR 766.11(a)) and revises it as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Provides training, equipment and resources; ensures incidents are investigated and trends reviewed; protects employees from retaliation for reporting or leaving an unsafe situation.
Receives safety reports, arranges coverage and follow-up, reassesses homes and plans, and decides on changes to the care arrangement.
Evaluates the home environment at assessment, records hazards and reports unsafe conditions.
Follow safe handling practices; carry ID; leave unsafe situations; report hazards, threats and injuries promptly.

documentation: Home environment findings in the assessment
Pre-visit risk notes in the clinical record
Employee safety training attendance records
Incident reports (SAF-02) and follow-up notes
Record of care arrangement changes after a safety incident
QI Committee minutes on safety trends

policies.title: Transporting Clients
policies.applies_to: Personal care aides, other employees who may drive or accompany patients, and the RN Director and office staff who authorize or schedule such trips
policies.purpose: To make sure that any time an employee transports a patient, it is authorized in the plan of care, is done safely, is covered by insurance and is documented.
policies.policy: Employees transport patients only if the plan of care authorizes it and the RN Director has approved the trip. The driver must hold a valid driver's license and the vehicle must be insured and in safe working order. Seatbelts are used for everyone, and child or adaptive restraints are used when needed. Aides do not transport patients in their own vehicles unless the agency's insurance covers it. Accidents are reported as incidents under SAF-02. Mileage reimbursement is handled under the agency's wage and hour policy (PER-09). Delivery of services is recorded in the clinical record (10 NYCRR 766.2(a)(2)), and the RN director's supervision includes reviewing that services are delivered as planned (10 NYCRR 766.5(b)).

definitions.definition: Driving a patient in a motor vehicle, as distinct from accompanying a patient on public transit, in a taxi or in a medical transport vehicle arranged by someone else.
A trip listed or described in the plan of care and approved by the RN Director, such as travel to a medical appointment or necessary errands, with the destination and purpose stated.
An agency-owned or agency-leased vehicle, or an employee's own vehicle for which the agency's insurance carrier has confirmed coverage in writing.

procedures: Transporting a patient is not part of the default aide duties. Before any trip, the RN confirms the plan of care authorizes it and records the purpose and likely destinations. The plan and the Aide Care Plan (SVC-08) must both include the task.

The RN Director approves each patient's transport need. The RN considers the patient's mobility, cognition, behavior, equipment, seating and restraint needs, whether the patient could use public or medical transport instead, and the aide's training. The RN records the decision.

Before an employee drives for the agency, office staff verify a valid driver's license, a current driving record check, and the agency's insurance carrier's approval. Office staff place copies in the personnel file (PER-08) and re-verify the license annually.

The employee must confirm the vehicle is in safe working order, registered, inspected and insured. For an agency vehicle, office staff keep maintenance records and the Administrator ensures regular inspection.

Aides may not use their own vehicles to transport patients unless the Administrator has confirmed in writing, before the trip, that the agency's insurance covers the vehicle and the driver. Otherwise the aide offers to arrange other transport (public, medical transport or family) through the RN Director.

Before departure, the driver checks the patient is comfortable, secures the wheelchair or equipment, makes sure every person wears a seatbelt, and uses child or adaptive restraints as required for the patient. The driver does not transport more people than the vehicle has seats and restraints.
The driver does not use a handheld phone while driving, does not smoke in the vehicle, and does not drive while impaired by alcohol, drugs or medication, or while too tired to drive safely.
The driver does not take a patient anywhere other than the authorized destination, does not leave the patient unattended in the vehicle, and stays with the patient as the plan of care requires.

If the patient becomes ill, behaves in a way that makes driving unsafe, or refuses to wear a seatbelt, the driver stops in a safe place, calls 911 if there is a medical emergency, and calls the RN Director. Emergency steps follow SVC-14.
After the trip, the aide documents the date, start and end times, destination, purpose and mileage in the task record (SVC-08), and reports any problems to the RN Director the same day.

If an accident occurs, the driver calls 911 if anyone may be injured, gets medical care for anyone hurt, exchanges information as the law requires, and calls the RN Director immediately. The RN Director notifies the Administrator, who ensures an incident report is filed (SAF-02) within the deadline in that policy, and who notifies the insurance carrier.
Mileage and travel time are reimbursed and paid according to PER-09. Office staff verify mileage logs before payment.
The RN Director reviews transport records during supervisory visits (SVC-10) and reports accidents and near misses to the QI Committee (GOV-04) quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Approves transport in the plan of care; assesses patient needs; reviews records and incidents.
Confirms insurance coverage; ensures driver verification and vehicle maintenance; reports accidents to the carrier.
Drive only on authorized trips; keep a valid license; use seatbelts and restraints; document and report trips and accidents.
Verify licenses and driving records; maintain vehicle records; verify mileage logs.

documentation: Plan of care entry authorizing transport
RN Director approval and patient transport assessment
Driver's license and driving record verification
Written insurance coverage confirmation
Vehicle inspection and maintenance records
Trip records (date, time, destination, purpose, mileage)
Incident reports (SAF-02) for any accident

policies.title: Personnel Policies, Qualifications, Job Descriptions and Performance Evaluations
policies.applies_to: All applicants and employees, the Administrator, the RN Director, supervisors and office staff
policies.purpose: To establish written personnel policies under which [AGENCY NAME] hires only qualified and verified staff, defines each job, and evaluates performance on a set schedule.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps written personnel policies and reviews them at least annually (10 NYCRR 766.11(a)). All staff must be qualified for the duties they are assigned. The agency employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care. Aide qualifications follow the definitions in 10 NYCRR 700.2 (see PER-02). The agency verifies identity before hire, and verifies employment history and references before the employee has patient contact (10 NYCRR 766.11(e)-(f)). The agency keeps a written job description for each position (10 NYCRR 766.11(j)) and performs an annual performance assessment that includes at least one in-home observation visit where applicable (10 NYCRR 766.11(k)). This policy meets the following Applicant Worksheet p.10 items: WS-PERS.1 (qualifications for all staff); WS-PERS.2 (verification of credentials); WS-PERS.4 (employment verification/references, two); WS-PERS.5 (personal identification); WS-PERS.6 (a signed and dated application); WS-PERS.7 (job descriptions for each position); and WS-PERS.8 (performance evaluations and frequency). Health screening, the Registry, criminal history record checks, orientation and in-service are covered in PER-06, PER-03, PER-04 and PER-05.

definitions.definition: Holds the license, certificate, training and demonstrated skill required for the assigned role, verified and documented before patient contact.
A professional license, registration, certificate or training completion that a position requires, for example an RN license or an approved aide training certificate.
Unexpired, government-issued photo identification, or other documents allowed by federal employment eligibility rules.
Any work in the patient's home or in person or by telephone with the patient or family that involves care or services.
A visit by the RN to the patient's home while the aide is working, to watch the aide's performance and compare it to the Aide Care Plan.

procedures: The Administrator reviews these personnel policies at least annually, records the date and any changes, and re-distributes revised policies to employees, who sign that they received them.

The Administrator writes a job description for every position (Administrator, RN Director, RN, office/scheduling staff, personal care aide, home health aide and any other position the agency uses). Each states title, reporting relationship, minimum qualifications, duties and responsibilities, and physical and training requirements. This addresses Worksheet item WS-PERS.7. The Administrator reviews descriptions annually.

Qualifications (Worksheet item WS-PERS.1): the minimum qualifications are in the job description. The Administrator: a person with the experience and education to run the agency as set in GOV-01. The RN Director and RNs: a current NYS RN license and registration. Aides: the training and Registry requirements in PER-02. Office staff: the skills listed in the job description. The agency hires no one who does not meet the qualifications.

Each applicant completes and signs and dates a written application. It lists work history, education, licenses and certificates, and at least two references. The signed and dated application goes in the personnel file. This addresses Worksheet item WS-PERS.6.

Before hire, the hiring manager checks the applicant's identity against acceptable government-issued photo identification, copies it, and records the date and the name of the person who checked it. The agency also completes federal employment eligibility verification at hire. This addresses Worksheet item WS-PERS.5.

Credential verification (Worksheet item WS-PERS.2): before hire, the hiring manager verifies every license or certificate the job requires. For an RN, verify the license and registration status with the NYS Education Department online. For aides, verify training under PER-02. The verification is printed or saved with its date and the verifier's name. Licenses are re-verified at each renewal date.

Employment history and references (Worksheet item WS-PERS.4): before the employee has any patient contact, the hiring manager verifies employment history and obtains at least two references or employment verifications, from prior employers where possible. The manager records the name and title of each person contacted, the date, the method, and the answers. If a prior employer will not respond after two documented tries, the manager obtains another reference and notes the reason.

The hiring manager runs the Home Care Registry check (PER-03) and the criminal history record check (PER-04), and confirms health requirements are met (PER-06), before assigning the employee to patient contact.

Offer letters state the job title, supervisor, and the conditions the employee must meet. No one begins patient contact until the Administrator or RN Director confirms in writing that all verifications and checks are complete.
New employees receive their job description and the personnel policies at orientation and sign that they received them (PER-05).

Performance evaluations (Worksheet item WS-PERS.8): each employee receives an initial evaluation after the first 90 days of employment and a written performance assessment at least once every 12 months. The RN Director evaluates clinical staff and aides. The Administrator evaluates office staff and the RN Director.

Annual assessments for aides and other staff who give care include at least one in-home observation visit by the RN (SVC-10), where applicable, to see how the employee follows the Aide Care Plan, communicates with the patient and handles safety and infection control. Evaluators also review attendance, documentation, patient and family feedback, complaints, competency results and in-service completion.

The evaluator discusses the evaluation with the employee, who signs it and may add comments. If performance is unsatisfactory, the evaluator documents a corrective plan with deadlines. The signed evaluation is filed in the personnel record (PER-08).
The Administrator tracks due dates for evaluations and reports overdue evaluations to the QI Committee (GOV-04) each quarter.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts personnel policies and ensures enough qualified staff are employed.
Reviews policies annually; keeps job descriptions current; approves hires; evaluates office staff and the RN Director.
Verifies clinical credentials; evaluates clinical staff and aides, including in-home observation; confirms qualifications before assignment.
Collect applications, verify identity, credentials and references, and file records.
Give accurate information; maintain credentials; take part in evaluations.

documentation: Signed and dated application
Identity verification record and copy of ID
Credential verifications (license, registration, training)
Reference and employment verification records (at least two)
Written job descriptions with signed acknowledgments
Initial and annual performance evaluations, with in-home observation record
Annual personnel policy review record

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Training Verification and Certification
policies.applies_to: Personal care aides, home health aides, advanced home health aides (if the agency uses them), the RN Director and the staff who hire and verify aides
policies.purpose: To make sure every aide who serves patients for [AGENCY NAME] has completed approved training, has been verified, and is listed correctly in the Home Care Registry before assignment.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assigns only aides who meet the qualifications in 10 NYCRR 700.2 and 10 NYCRR 766.11(b), and whose information is in the Home Care Registry as Public Health Law §3613 provides. For Medicaid personal care, a personal care aide needs either a DOH-approved home health aide program or the 40-hour personal care aide basic training (18 NYCRR 505.14(e)), completed within 3 months of hire, and 3 hours of in-service semiannually. Home health aides complete a basic home health aide program or an approved equivalency exam. Before assigning an aide, the agency reviews the training materials to confirm training from a DOH- or SED-approved program, including the Registry aide profile and, if available, the training certificate (DOH DAL DHCBS 20-05). The certificate and verification are kept in the personnel record.

definitions.definition: An aide who has completed a DOH-approved home health aide program or the 40-hour personal care aide basic training and who provides personal care services under RN supervision.
An aide who has completed a DOH-approved basic home health aide training program or has passed an approved equivalency exam.
An HHA who has completed additional approved training and whose AHHA status appears in the Registry. [AGENCY NAME] uses AHHAs only if its license and policies are amended to do so.

The state registry of home care services workers established by Public Health Law §3613, which holds each worker's name, address, gender, date of birth and training program, and shows AHHA status and any limitation or revocation.
A training program approved by DOH or by the State Education Department.

procedures: Before an offer is made, the hiring manager asks the aide applicant for the training certificate and the name of the approved program, and for the dates of the training.

The hiring manager reviews the available training materials to confirm the training came from a DOH- or SED-approved program. The materials must include the Home Care Registry aide profile, and must include the training certificate if it is available (DOH DAL DHCBS 20-05).

The hiring manager looks the aide up in the Home Care Registry and prints or saves the aide profile with the date. The profile should show the aide's name, address, gender, date of birth and training program (PHL §3613). The manager checks that the information matches the aide's identification (PER-01).

If the aide is not in the Registry or the information does not match, the hiring manager does not assign the aide to patients. The manager contacts the training program and the Registry for correction, records each contact, and tells the RN Director.

For a PCA, the manager confirms completion of either a DOH-approved home health aide program or the 40-hour PCA basic training (18 NYCRR 505.14(e)). For an HHA, the manager confirms completion of the approved basic HHA program or an approved equivalency exam (10 NYCRR 700.2).

The agency's practice is to hire only aides who have completed training before assignment. If the agency ever hires an aide who still has to complete required PCA training, the RN Director records the date of hire, tracks the 3-month completion deadline, and assigns that person only to tasks the RN has determined are appropriate. The RN performs an in-home supervisory visit with return demonstration of those tasks at the first service visit (10 NYCRR 766.5(d)(1)). A person who does not finish by the deadline is removed from patient assignment.

The RN Director checks that the aide's training covers the tasks on the patient's Aide Care Plan. If it does not, or the aide lacks documented training and experience in a task, the RN gives in-home instruction and has the aide return-demonstrate before the aide does the task alone (10 NYCRR 766.5(d)(1); SVC-10).

For advanced home health aides, if the agency uses them, the manager confirms the AHHA status in the Registry and checks that no limitation or revocation is noted. The agency provides RN home visits at least every two weeks for AHHAs (10 NYCRR 766.5(e)). If the agency does not use AHHAs, the manager does not assign any AHHA to AHHA tasks.

The manager checks all other hiring requirements before assignment: identity and references (PER-01), criminal history record check (PER-04), health screening (PER-06), and orientation and competency (PER-05). The RN Director signs a Qualification Checklist stating that the aide is cleared for assignment.
The office staff put copies of the certificate, the Registry profile, the verification notes and the signed checklist in the personnel record (PER-08).

The RN Director tracks in-service hours for each aide. Each aide must complete at least 3 hours of in-service semiannually for Medicaid personal care, and the annual in-service totals at least 6 hours for PCAs and 12 hours for HHAs (10 NYCRR 766.11(i); PER-05). The RN Director records hours in the personnel record and follows up with any aide who is behind.
The office staff check the Registry for each aide's profile at least once a year, and again if the aide's name or address changes. They record the date and resolve any discrepancy with the Registry.
The agency does not allow an aide to use a title or do tasks beyond their training. An aide may not be called an HHA or AHHA unless the Registry and training records support it.
The Administrator reports any aide who does not meet qualifications, and any correction of Registry data, to the QI Committee at least quarterly (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Confirms aide qualifications and task training; signs the Qualification Checklist; tracks in-service; provides in-home instruction and return demonstration.
Ensures the verification process is followed; decides whether the agency uses AHHAs and ensures the license and policies support it.
Collect and verify certificates, check the Registry, and file records.
Provide accurate training information; keep copies of certificates; complete in-service on time.

documentation: Training certificate or program completion record
Home Care Registry aide profile with date of check
Verification notes (program approval, contacts with program or Registry)
Qualification Checklist signed by RN Director
3-month training completion tracking, if used
In-service hours log
Annual Registry re-check record

policies.title: Home Care Worker Registry
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Director, Personnel/HR Coordinator, Scheduler, and the designated Home Care Registry users
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] uses the NYS Home Care Worker Registry correctly. Every aide must be verified in the Registry before providing services, and the agency's employment information must be posted, corrected and ended on time. The policy implements 10 NYCRR Part 403 and Public Health Law §3613.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is a licensed home care services agency under PHL Article 36 and is subject to 10 NYCRR Part 403. This written policy implements Part 403 as required by §403.3(b). The agency designates at least two individuals to access and enter data in the Registry (§403.3(a)). Only those designated individuals may submit data (§403.3(c)).

This policy meets the following items on the DOH Applicant Worksheet, p.12:
- WS-HCR.1 (Home Care Registry policy/procedure): the Registry must be accessed for any worker who began training on or after September 25, 2009. See Procedures 3 to 4.
- WS-HCR.2: a worker may not begin to provide services until the Registry has been accessed. See Procedures 4 and 6.
- WS-HCR.3: a worker may not begin to provide services until their information has been posted to the Registry. A person trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 may not provide services until posted (§403.5). See Procedures 5 and 6.
- WS-HCR.4: the worker's employment information, including the start date, is posted within 10 business days of starting employment with the agency (§403.5(a)(6), as described in DOH DAL 19-21). See Procedures 7 to 9.
- WS-HCR.5: the agency updates the Registry within 10 business days with any correction requested by the worker. See Procedure 10.
- WS-HCR.6: the agency updates the Registry within 10 business days of the worker's termination. See Procedure 11.

The Registry holds the information PHL §3613 requires for each worker who completes a state-approved training program. That information is name, address, gender, date of birth and program. It also shows advanced home health aide status and any limitation or revocation of that status. The agency treats the Registry as the source for confirming that a worker's training is posted. The agency does not assign any aide to a patient on the basis of a training certificate alone.

definitions.definition: The NYS DOH database established under PHL §3613 and 10 NYCRR Part 403 that lists home care workers who completed a state-approved training program and records their employment information.
A person the agency has designated in writing to access and enter data in the Registry under §403.3(a). The agency always has at least two.
The first date the worker provides services for the agency. The 10-business-day posting period runs from this date.
Monday through Friday, excluding legal holidays.
The worker's training record appears in the Registry (entered by the training program) and the agency's employment information has been entered.

procedures: Designation. The Administrator designates in writing at least two Registry users: [REGISTRY DESIGNEE 1 NAME] and [REGISTRY DESIGNEE 2 NAME]. The signed designation is kept in the Administrative Policy file and on the Communication Directory (GOV-07). This meets Part 403.3(a).

Access control. Designees obtain Registry access through their individual Health Commerce System accounts (GOV-07). They do not share credentials. No one else enters or changes Registry data (§403.3(c)). The Administrator reviews the designee list at least annually and whenever a designee leaves or changes roles. The Administrator names a replacement within 5 business days so that two designees are always in place.

Training-date check (WS-HCR.1). Before an aide is scheduled, the Personnel/HR Coordinator records the date the aide began training from the training certificate (see PER-02). If the aide began training on or after September 25, 2009, the Registry check in Procedure 4 is mandatory. For aides who began training earlier, qualifications are verified under PER-02, and the designee still searches the Registry and records the result.

Registry access before assignment (WS-HCR.2). A designee accesses the Registry and searches for the aide by name and date of birth. The designee saves or prints the result with the date, time and designee's name and places it in the personnel file (PER-08). This is done before the aide's first assignment.

Posting check (WS-HCR.3). The designee confirms that the aide's training appears as posted. If the aide does not appear or is not posted, the aide is not assigned and provides no services. The Personnel/HR Coordinator contacts the training program and the aide to have the training posted. The check is repeated after the program reports the posting. The aide stays unassigned until the designee records a successful posting.

Assignment hold. The designee signs a "Registry Cleared" entry in the personnel file and in the scheduling system. The Scheduler may not assign any aide trained on or after 9/25/2009 who lacks that entry (see SVC-12). The RN Director may not authorize a first visit without it.

Employment posting deadline (WS-HCR.4). The designee posts the agency's employment information, including the start date, within 10 business days after the aide begins providing services (§403.5(a)(6)). As an internal standard, the designee posts within 5 business days. The Scheduler sends the start date to the designee on the day of the aide's first visit.

Posting content. The designee enters the employment information the Registry requires. If the agency uses advanced home health aides, the designee also enters or checks the AHHA status indicator, as PHL §3613 provides.

Confirmation. After each posting, the designee prints or saves the confirmation and files it in the personnel file with the date posted. The Administrator reviews a posting log each month. The log shows start date, date accessed, date posted and the business-day count.

Worker-requested corrections (WS-HCR.5). If a worker reports an error in Registry information, the receiving staff member logs the request on the Registry Correction Log with the date received and gives it to a designee the same business day. The designee makes the update, or submits it as the Registry requires, within 10 business days of the request. The designee confirms the correction with the worker and files the confirmation.

Termination update (WS-HCR.6). On any separation, whether resignation, termination or end of assignment, the Personnel/HR Coordinator tells a designee by the next business day. The designee updates the Registry within 10 business days of the termination date, records the update date in the personnel file and attaches the confirmation.

Monthly reconciliation. The designee compares the active aide roster (see SAF-05) against the Registry. Any aide who is not posted, any missing employment posting and any separated worker not yet updated is corrected immediately. The Administrator signs the reconciliation.
Rehires and returns. If a former aide returns, a designee repeats the Registry check in Procedures 3 to 5 and posts new employment information within 10 business days of the new start date.

Limitations or revocations. If the Registry shows a limitation or revocation of advanced home health aide status, or any other adverse information, the designee notifies the Administrator and RN Director the same day. The worker is removed from any task or assignment the limitation affects until the RN Director and Administrator approve a plan.

Policy review. The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually with the personnel policies (10 NYCRR §766.11(a)). The review checks that it still matches Part 403 and the DOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool.

responsibilities.duty: Designate at least two Registry users, keep the designation current, review the monthly reconciliation and enforce the no-service-until-posted rule.
Access the Registry before assignment, confirm the posting, post employment information, make corrections and termination updates on time, and keep confirmations.
Record training dates, request posting from training programs and notify designees of starts and separations.
Assign only aides with a "Registry Cleared" entry and report first-visit dates.
Confirm Registry clearance before authorizing a first visit and act on any Registry limitation or revocation.

documentation: Written designation of Registry users
Registry access and search confirmation with date, time and designee name, kept in the personnel file
"Registry Cleared" entry in the personnel file and scheduling system
Employment posting confirmation and posting log showing business-day count
Registry Correction Log and confirmations
Termination update confirmation
Monthly reconciliation signed by the Administrator

policies.title: Criminal History Record Check (CHRC) and Background Checks
policies.applies_to: Administrator, CHRC Authorized Persons, Personnel/HR Coordinator, RN Director, supervisors and all prospective employees
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who works for [AGENCY NAME] in a role subject to Part 402 has a criminal history record check requested and handled on time. The policy also protects employee rights and confidentiality, and requires that people awaiting a DOH determination are supervised and the supervision is documented.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] requests a criminal history record check (CHRC) through DOH for each prospective employee, as required by 10 NYCRR §402.6(a) and Part 402. The agency also verifies identity, employment history and references before patient contact, and runs the CHRC as 10 NYCRR §766.11(e)-(f) requires. The agency does not decide for itself whether a criminal record disqualifies a person. It follows DOH's determination.

This policy meets the following items on the DOH Applicant Worksheet, p.11 (and p.10 for WS-PERS.3):
- WS-CHRC.1 (CHRC policy/procedure): designation of CHRC authorized persons. See Procedure 1.
- WS-CHRC.2: confidentiality. See Procedures 4 and 17.
- WS-CHRC.3: who is subject to a CHRC. See Procedure 2.
- WS-CHRC.4: employee rights including informed consent. See Procedure 3.
- WS-CHRC.5: process for requesting and obtaining fingerprints, including timeframes. See Procedures 5 to 9.
- WS-CHRC.6: supervision of temporary personnel awaiting determinations. See Procedures 10 to 11.
- WS-CHRC.7: documentation of supervision. See Procedure 12.
- WS-CHRC.8: procedures for Hold in Abeyance, Pending or Final Determination letters. See Procedures 13 to 15.
- WS-CHRC.9: process for reporting terminations and separations to the Department. See Procedure 16.
- WS-CHRC.10: retention, confidentiality and separation of personnel records. See Procedure 17.
- WS-PERS.3 (background checks of paraprofessional staff): see Procedure 18.

definitions.definition: The criminal history record check that DOH conducts under 10 NYCRR Part 402 on prospective employees, using fingerprints.
A person the agency designates in writing who may sign the DOH CHRC form and submit requests.
Permission under §402.6(d) to work with patients pending CHRC results. The person must be supervised under §402.4.

definitions.term: Hold in Abeyance / Pending / Final Determination letter
definitions.definition: Letters from DOH about the status or outcome of a CHRC. An abeyance or pending letter means no final decision has been made. A final determination states DOH's decision.
Monday through Friday, excluding legal holidays.

procedures: Designation (WS-CHRC.1). The Administrator designates in writing the CHRC Authorized Persons: [CHRC AUTHORIZED PERSON 1 NAME] and [CHRC AUTHORIZED PERSON 2 NAME]. Only these persons sign the DOH CHRC form. The designation is kept on file and updated whenever a designee changes.

Who is subject (WS-CHRC.3). The Personnel/HR Coordinator requests a CHRC for each prospective employee, as §402.6(a) and Part 402 require. This includes personal care aides, home health aides, nurses and other persons whose roles Part 402 covers. When there is doubt whether a role is covered, the Administrator confirms with DOH before the person starts and records the answer.

Informed consent and employee rights (WS-CHRC.4). Before fingerprinting, the Personnel/HR Coordinator gives the applicant a written explanation of the check. It covers why it is required, that DOH makes the determination, that results are confidential, and how the applicant can review the information used and seek correction through the DOH or State fingerprint-record process. The applicant signs consent, and a copy is kept. The applicant is told that a refusal to consent means the check cannot be completed and the agency cannot employ the person in a covered role.

Confidentiality at intake (WS-CHRC.2). Applicants are told that CHRC results are disclosed only to Authorized Persons and the Administrator. Staff do not discuss results with anyone else, including coworkers, patients or other employers.

Identity documents (WS-CHRC.5). The applicant presents two IDs. One must be government-issued with a signature, and at least one must have a photo (§402.6(c)(1)). The Authorized Person records the IDs checked and the date.

Fingerprinting. The Authorized Person gives the applicant the DOH fingerprinting instructions and the form. The Authorized Person records the date the fingerprints were taken. If the applicant is fingerprinted at a vendor, the applicant gives the date to the Authorized Person the same day.

Submission deadline. An Authorized Person signs the DOH CHRC form. The form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days, excluding weekends and legal holidays, after the prints were taken (§402.6(b)). The Authorized Person records the submission date and keeps proof of mailing or electronic filing.

Rejected prints. If DOH reports that the prints were rejected, the Authorized Person tells the applicant the same business day. The applicant is re-fingerprinted and the new submission goes to DOH within 14 days of the notice (§402.6(c)(3)). The Authorized Person tracks the deadline.
Expedited review. If the person already has a prior CHRC determination or a pending submission, the Authorized Person requests expedited review as §402.6(e) allows and keeps the correspondence.

Temporary approval (WS-CHRC.6). A person may begin work under temporary approval only if the Administrator documents the approval (§402.6(d)). All other pre-hire verifications under §766.11(e)-(f) must be complete first. The person works only with the supervision required by §402.4 until a final determination is received.

Supervision assignment. The RN Director names a supervisor for each person on temporary approval. The supervisor monitors the person's work on patient care and other duties according to §402.4, and reviews the person's work with the RN Director at least [WEEKLY].

Supervision documentation (WS-CHRC.7). The supervisor completes a Temporary Personnel Supervision Log. For each period it records the person, supervisor, dates, activities supervised and any concerns, and it is signed and dated. Logs are kept in the CHRC file until a final determination is received and then retained with the personnel records.
Letters received (WS-CHRC.8). The Authorized Person logs the date of every DOH letter on the day it arrives and gives it to the Administrator. The Administrator reads it the same business day.

Hold in Abeyance or Pending letter. The agency follows the instructions in the letter and supplies any requested information within the stated time. The person remains subject to the §402.4 supervision for as long as the letter's status stands. The person is not allowed unsupervised patient contact. The Authorized Person records every action taken.

Final Determination letter. The Administrator reads the letter and records the date and outcome. If DOH permits the person's employment, the letter is filed and temporary supervision ends. If DOH's determination does not permit employment in the covered role, the Administrator takes the action the letter requires immediately, removes the person from patient contact, and notifies the Personnel/HR Coordinator and the Scheduler. The agency does not override a DOH determination.

Reporting terminations and separations (WS-CHRC.9). When a person with a pending or temporary-approval CHRC leaves the agency, or any person subject to a CHRC separates, the Personnel/HR Coordinator tells an Authorized Person by the next business day. The Authorized Person reports the termination or separation to DOH promptly in the manner and within the time DOH's current instructions require. The date reported, and proof of the report, are filed in the personnel record.

Retention and separation of records (WS-CHRC.10). CHRC forms, consents, letters and logs are kept in a locked CHRC file or restricted electronic folder, separate from the general personnel file. Only the Administrator and Authorized Persons may open it. Each file keeps an entry showing the CHRC was completed. Records are kept as personnel records for at least 3 years after the person separates (10 NYCRR §766.12(a)(3), see PER-08). They are then destroyed securely.

Background checks of paraprofessional staff (WS-PERS.3). Before any aide has patient contact, the Personnel/HR Coordinator completes and documents: identity verification (§766.11(e)); employment history and reference verification (§766.11(f)); the CHRC under this policy; the Home Care Registry check (PER-03); and any exclusion screening required by the Compliance Program (GOV-05). A checklist signed by the Personnel/HR Coordinator is kept in each aide's personnel file.

responsibilities.duty: Designate Authorized Persons, approve temporary approvals, review every DOH letter and act on determinations.
Sign and submit CHRC forms and fingerprints on time, verify IDs, track rejected prints and letters, and report separations to DOH.
Obtain consent, complete background verifications, maintain the CHRC file and notify Authorized Persons of separations.
Assign supervisors for temporary personnel, ensure supervision under §402.4 occurs and complete the Supervision Log.
Give consent, present valid IDs, be fingerprinted promptly and re-submit within 14 days if prints are rejected.

documentation: Written designation of CHRC Authorized Persons
Signed informed consent and rights notice
DOH CHRC form, ID record and fingerprint date
Proof of submission to DOH within 10 business days
Rejected-print notice and re-submission record
Temporary approval record
Temporary Personnel Supervision Log
DOH Hold in Abeyance, Pending and Final Determination letters and action log
Termination or separation report to DOH
Background check checklist for aides (identity, employment history, references, CHRC, Registry)

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
policies.applies_to: All personnel, with emphasis on personal care aides, home health aides, RNs, the RN Director, the Administrator and the Training Coordinator
policies.purpose: To make sure every worker is oriented before patient contact, shown to be competent for the tasks assigned, and trained again each year. The policy gives the required in-service hours and the required topics.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides orientation to all personnel before they have patient contact, and annual in-service training, as 10 NYCRR §766.11(i) requires. Bloodborne pathogen training is given at hire and yearly (§766.11(l)). Training is documented along with a competency check. For Medicaid personal care, the agency also applies the aide training and in-service rules in 18 NYCRR §505.14(e), as summarized in the agency's regulatory research. The Administrator confirms the current text of that subdivision before relying on the hours below.

This policy meets the following items on the DOH Applicant Worksheet:
- WS-OT.1 (Orientation and Training policy/procedure), p.11: training on agency policy and procedures. See Procedure 3.
- WS-OT.2: HIV and bloodborne pathogens exposure plan. See Procedure 4.
- WS-OT.3: infection control, universal precautions and use of protective equipment. See Procedure 5.
- WS-OT.4: HIV confidentiality and disclosure. See Procedure 6.
- WS-OT.5: yearly mandatory in-servicing. See Procedures 11 to 14.
- WS-OT.6: HIPAA, including the training duty in 45 CFR 164.530. See Procedure 7.
- WS-OT.7: personal care aides participate in 6 hours of in-service per year; home health aides, if the agency is approved to use them, 12 hours. See Procedure 11.
- WS-PCA.9 (Applicant Worksheet p.2): 6 hours of in-service training yearly. See Procedure 11.

Orientation also covers the emergency plan (SAF-05 and SAF-06).

definitions.definition: Training given to every new worker before patient contact, on the topics listed in this policy.
Continuing education given each year to aides and other personnel: at least 6 hours for personal care aides, 12 for home health aides and 18 for advanced home health aides (§766.11(i)).
A documented evaluation, by the RN Director or an RN designee, that a worker can perform assigned tasks correctly. It includes return demonstration of skills.
Twelve months beginning on the worker's date of hire, unless the agency adopts a uniform calendar year in writing.
The worker performs the task while the RN observes and records whether it was done correctly.

procedures: Responsibility. The Administrator appoints a Training Coordinator, [TRAINING COORDINATOR NAME], who maintains the orientation curriculum, schedules in-service, tracks hours and reports to the QI Committee (GOV-04). The RN Director approves all clinical content.
Timing. Orientation is completed before the worker's first patient contact. The Scheduler may not assign a worker whose orientation checklist is incomplete (see SVC-12).

Agency policies and procedures (WS-OT.1). Orientation covers the agency's policies and procedures, including: patient rights (CR-01); the aide's scope of tasks (SVC-01); the aide care plan and reporting changes (SVC-08); abuse and neglect reporting (SAF-01); incident reporting (SAF-02); documentation and timekeeping (SVC-13); and staff conduct (PER-10). The worker signs that they received and reviewed the policy manual or the sections for their job.

HIV and bloodborne pathogens exposure plan (WS-OT.2). The worker is trained on the agency's exposure control program, including exposure-management steps, reporting and follow-up (SAF-04). This training is given at hire and repeated yearly as §766.11(l) and 29 CFR 1910.1030 require. Training is given at no cost and during paid time.

Infection control, universal precautions and protective equipment (WS-OT.3). The worker is trained on hand hygiene, universal precautions, barriers, the proper use, removal and disposal of PPE, and cleaning of equipment (SAF-03). The worker demonstrates correct glove and PPE use before the competency check is signed.

HIV confidentiality and disclosure (WS-OT.4). The worker is trained on the confidentiality of HIV-related information and the limited circumstances in which it may be disclosed. The worker is told that confidential HIV-related information may not be shared with family, other staff or others without authorization, and who in the agency answers questions about disclosure (see CR-04).

HIPAA (WS-OT.6). The worker is trained on the agency's privacy policies, including protection of patient information, minimum necessary use, device and record handling and breach reporting, as 45 CFR 164.530 requires (CR-04). The training date is recorded.
Emergency plan. The worker is oriented to the emergency preparedness plan, the call-down tree and what to do in the patient's home during an emergency (SAF-05, SAF-06, SVC-14).

Competency evaluation. After orientation the RN Director or an RN designee evaluates each aide on each task on the aide's care plan. For aides who lack documented training and experience in a task, the RN is present at the initial service visit and requires return demonstration (10 NYCRR §766.5(d)(1)). The RN records the date, the task, and "competent" or "needs more training." No aide performs a task until competent.
Required observations and reports. During in-home supervision the RN instructs the aide on the observations and written reports required for each patient (§766.5(d)(3)) and records this (see SVC-10).

In-service hours (WS-OT.5, WS-OT.7, WS-PCA.9). Each personal care aide completes at least 6 hours of in-service per training year. Each home health aide, if the agency is approved to use them, completes at least 12 hours. Each advanced home health aide, if the agency uses them, completes at least 18 hours (§766.11(i)). Hours are tracked individually by the Training Coordinator.

Medicaid personal care in-service. For aides who provide Medicaid personal care, the Training Coordinator also tracks 3 hours of in-service each half of the training year, in line with 18 NYCRR §505.14(e). The Coordinator schedules sessions so that the two 3-hour sessions satisfy the semiannual duty. Any hours required in addition are tracked separately.

Annual content. Every year's in-service includes at least: bloodborne pathogens and exposure control; infection control; HIV confidentiality; HIPAA; abuse and neglect reporting; emergency preparedness; and topics the QI Committee or the RN Director identifies from supervision findings, incidents and complaints.

Tracking and make-up. The Training Coordinator reviews hours quarterly. Staff who are 30 days or more behind schedule receive written notice and a make-up date within 30 days. An aide who has not completed required hours by the end of the training year is not scheduled until the hours are made up.

Documentation. For each session the Coordinator keeps a sign-in sheet (title, date, hours, presenter and content), a post-test or competency check, and an entry in the worker's personnel record (PER-08).
Review. The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually with the personnel policies (§766.11(a)).

responsibilities.duty: Appoint the Training Coordinator, provide resources and make sure no untrained worker has patient contact.
Approve clinical content, perform or delegate competency evaluations, and instruct aides on required observations and reports.
Schedule orientation and in-service, track hours, keep records and report gaps.
File training records in personnel records and confirm completion before first assignment.
Assign only workers with completed orientation and competency evaluation.
Attend training, pass competency checks and follow what they are taught.

documentation: Orientation checklist signed by worker and trainer
Policy acknowledgment
Bloodborne pathogen, infection control, HIV confidentiality and HIPAA training records
Competency evaluation with return demonstration
In-service sign-in sheets, tests and annual hours log (6 / 12 / 18 hours; 3 hours semiannually for Medicaid personal care)
Quarterly tracking report and make-up notices

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All personnel with direct patient contact, the RN Director, the Personnel/HR Coordinator and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To protect patients and staff by assessing the health of personnel before patient contact and each year, and by documenting immunity, TB screening and influenza status, while keeping health information confidential.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] assesses the health status of all personnel before they assume duties (10 NYCRR §766.11(c)) and each year for personnel with direct patient contact (§766.11(d)). Health records are kept separate and confidential (§766.11(g)). The agency complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act: health inquiries are made only after a conditional offer, are job-related, are applied to all employees in the same job, and are accommodated reasonably.

This policy meets the following items on the DOH Applicant Worksheet, p.10:
- WS-PH.1 (Personnel Health Requirements policy/procedure): pre-employment and annual health assessments. See Procedures 1 to 3 and 12.
- WS-PH.2: the health status of all new personnel is assessed and documented before assuming patient care duties. See Procedures 2 to 3 and 11.
- WS-PH.3: the statement that the prospective employee is free from impairment. See Procedure 4.
- WS-PH.4: documentation of rubella, measles (born on or after January 1, 1957), influenza, tuberculin skin test or blood assay, and annual health assessment. See Procedures 5 to 10.

definitions.definition: A review by a licensed health care practitioner of an employee's health status, including the items required by §766.11(c)-(d), documented in writing.

A signed statement that the person is free from impairment which is of potential risk to the patient or might interfere with the performance of his or her duties, including habituation or addiction to depressants, stimulants, narcotics, alcohol or drugs or substances which may alter the individual's behavior.
A tuberculin skin test or an interferon-gamma release (blood) assay.
Providing hands-on care or entering a patient's home or care area to deliver or supervise services.

procedures: Conditional offer. The Personnel/HR Coordinator makes health requirements known in the offer letter. Health inquiries and examination are done only after a conditional offer of employment, consistently with the ADA.

Assessment before duties (WS-PH.1, WS-PH.2). The new employee has a health assessment by a licensed practitioner ([HEALTH PROVIDER / CLINIC]) or presents one done within [90] days before hire. The assessment is completed and documented before the employee assumes any patient care duties. The Scheduler may not assign an employee without a "Health Cleared" entry from the RN Director.

Content of the assessment. The assessment states whether the employee is able to perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation, and records the TB and immunity items in Procedures 5 to 9.

Free-from-impairment statement (WS-PH.3). Before starting, the employee signs a statement that he or she is "free from impairment which is of potential risk to the patient or might interfere with the performance of his/her duties, including habituation or addiction to depressants, stimulants, narcotics, alcohol or drugs or substance which may alter the individual's behavior." The statement is repeated annually (Procedure 12).

Rubella (WS-PH.4). The record shows proof of rubella immunity: documented vaccination or a positive titer. If proof is missing, the practitioner determines vaccination or testing, and the RN Director and Administrator decide on assignment until the record is complete.
Measles (WS-PH.4). For employees born on or after January 1, 1957, the record shows proof of measles immunity: documented vaccination or a positive titer. The same follow-up in Procedure 5 applies.
TB risk assessment and symptom evaluation (WS-PH.4). Before employment, the practitioner completes a TB risk assessment and a symptom evaluation (cough, fever, weight loss, night sweats).
TB test (WS-PH.4). Before employment, the employee has a TB test (skin test or blood assay). The result and date are recorded. The test is repeated annually (§766.11(d)).

Positive test or symptoms. An employee with a positive TB test or TB symptoms is referred to a practitioner for evaluation, including chest imaging as the practitioner decides. The employee does not have patient contact until a practitioner documents that he or she is free from infectious TB. The Administrator reports to the local health department as required.
Influenza (WS-PH.4). The record documents the employee's influenza vaccination status or the signed mask election, as PER-07 requires.

Compliance before patient care. The RN Director reviews each file for completeness (impairment statement, rubella, measles if applicable, TB, influenza status) and signs the "Health Cleared" entry before the first assignment.

Annual assessment (WS-PH.1). Every year, each employee with direct patient contact has a health status assessment, a TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test, an updated influenza status and a renewed free-from-impairment statement. The Personnel/HR Coordinator sends reminders 60 days before each due date. An employee who has not completed the annual requirements by the due date is not scheduled until they are complete.

Reasonable accommodation. An employee who needs an accommodation or who cannot do the essential functions of the job is referred to the Administrator. The Administrator reviews the request with the practitioner's recommendation. Accommodation is considered under the ADA. The agency does not ask about a disability beyond what is job-related.
Illness reporting. Employees must report symptoms of communicable disease to the RN Director before a shift. The RN Director decides on work restrictions under the infection control policy (SAF-03).

Confidentiality (§766.11(g)). Health records are kept in a locked file or restricted electronic folder separate from the personnel file. Only the Administrator, the RN Director and the Personnel/HR Coordinator may access them. The personnel file holds only a clearance entry with dates. Health records are never given to patients, coworkers or outside parties unless the law requires.
Tracking. The Personnel/HR Coordinator keeps a health compliance tracker with due dates and reports overdue items monthly to the Administrator and QI Committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Make sure no employee provides patient care without health clearance, and decide on accommodations.
Review health files, sign the Health Cleared entry and decide on work restrictions for illness.
Collect and file health records separately, send reminders and maintain the compliance tracker.
Perform the health assessment, TB screening and immunity review.
Complete assessments on time, sign the impairment statement, report symptoms and give accurate information.

documentation: Pre-employment health assessment
Signed free-from-impairment statement (initial and annual)
Rubella and measles immunity records
TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test results (initial and annual)
Influenza vaccination or mask election record
Annual health assessment
"Health Cleared" entry in the personnel file
Health compliance tracker

policies.title: Influenza Vaccination and Mask Requirement
policies.applies_to: All personnel; the mask requirement applies to unvaccinated personnel with direct patient contact
policies.purpose: To reduce the spread of influenza to patients and staff by documenting the influenza vaccination status of all personnel and requiring education, supervision and a surgical or procedure mask for unvaccinated personnel with direct patient contact during influenza season.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] documents the influenza vaccination status of all personnel, as 10 NYCRR §766.11(d) requires. Personnel with direct patient contact who are not vaccinated must wear a surgical or procedure mask during influenza season. The agency educates them and supervises compliance. Influenza season is the period the New York State Commissioner of Health determines each year. The agency follows the Commissioner's announcement and does not set its own season. The Administrator confirms the current text of the state's influenza-mask rule before updating this policy or quoting it.

This policy meets the following items on the DOH Applicant Worksheet, p.11:
- WS-FLU.1 (Influenza Vaccination policy/procedure): the influenza season as determined by the Commissioner. See Procedures 1 to 2.
- WS-FLU.2: documentation of the vaccination status of all personnel. See Procedures 3 to 6.
- WS-FLU.3: procedures for unvaccinated personnel with direct patient contact, including supervision. See Procedures 9 to 12.
- WS-FLU.4: education and wearing of a surgical or procedure mask for all unvaccinated personnel with direct patient contact. See Procedures 7 to 10.

definitions.definition: The period of the year designated by the Commissioner of Health, announced to providers, during which the mask requirement applies.
A documented record that the person received the current seasonal influenza vaccine, was granted a medical exemption, or declined the vaccine.
A disposable, fluid-resistant mask that covers the nose and mouth and is not a cloth mask.
Providing hands-on care to a patient or being in the patient's home or care area in the course of providing or supervising services.

procedures: Season notice (WS-FLU.1). The Administrator monitors DOH notices received through the Health Commerce System (GOV-07) and records the dates the Commissioner announces the start and end of influenza season. The Administrator tells all personnel in writing within 2 business days of the announcement.

Annual cycle. Each year before the season, the Personnel/HR Coordinator offers the influenza vaccine, or gives information on where to get it, at no cost to the employee when practicable. The agency encourages vaccination.

Status for all personnel (WS-FLU.2). The Personnel/HR Coordinator collects and records the vaccination status of every employee, including office staff, at hire and each year. Status is recorded as: vaccinated (with date and source), medical exemption (with practitioner documentation), or declined.

Proof. Acceptable proof is a vaccination record, a pharmacy or provider receipt, or a signed attestation naming the date and place. The employee gives proof within [14] days of the season notice or within 14 days of hire.
Status list. The Personnel/HR Coordinator keeps a current status list for all personnel and updates it whenever proof is received. The list is kept with the confidential health records (PER-06).
Hired in season. Staff hired during the season complete the status form and, if unvaccinated, begin wearing masks on their first day of direct patient contact.

Education (WS-FLU.4). Every unvaccinated employee with direct patient contact receives education before the season on influenza transmission, the benefits of vaccination, correct mask use and hand hygiene. The employee signs that he or she received the education. The RN Director or RN designee gives the education.

Mask requirement (WS-FLU.4). During influenza season, every unvaccinated employee with direct patient contact wears a surgical or procedure mask whenever in the patient's home or care area, and while traveling with a patient. The agency supplies the masks at no cost.

Correct use. The mask covers the nose and mouth. It is changed when wet, soiled or damaged, and between patients. Hands are washed before and after handling the mask. Masks are disposed of as the infection control policy provides (SAF-03).

Supervision (WS-FLU.3). The RN Director supervises mask use. RN supervisors check mask use at every in-home supervisory visit during the season (SVC-10) and record compliance. Patients and family members may also report concerns to the agency, and the Administrator reviews them.

Noncompliance. An employee who fails to wear a mask is counseled by the RN Director the same day. A second failure is documented in a written warning under the progressive discipline policy (PER-10). Repeated noncompliance may lead to removal from direct patient contact and further action.

Changing status. An employee who is vaccinated mid-season gives proof to the Personnel/HR Coordinator. The status list is updated and the mask requirement ends once proof is accepted, unless DOH directs otherwise.
End of season. When the Commissioner ends the season, the Administrator tells all personnel in writing within 2 business days.
Reporting to QI. The Administrator reports the percentage of personnel with documented status, the vaccination rate and mask compliance findings to the QI Committee each year (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Track the Commissioner's season announcements, notify staff and make sure the mask requirement is enforced.
Provide education, supervise mask use and counsel noncompliance.
Collect and record vaccination status for all personnel and keep it confidential.
Check and document mask use during supervisory visits.
Report vaccination status, complete education and wear the mask when required.

documentation: Record of the Commissioner's season announcement and staff notice
Vaccination status list for all personnel, with proof or exemption documentation
Signed education record for unvaccinated direct-care staff
Mask-use checks recorded on supervisory visit forms
Counseling and warning records
Annual report to the QI Committee

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Personnel/HR Coordinator, RN Director, payroll staff and anyone who accesses personnel records
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps complete, accurate and secure personnel records, keeps health records separate and confidential, keeps required records for the required time, and keeps a current listing of all personnel at the principal office.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel record for each employee. Under 10 NYCRR §766.11(g), the record holds verifications, licenses, evaluations and employment dates. Health records are kept separate and confidential. Time and payment records are kept (§766.11(h)). Personnel records are kept for at least 3 years after the employee separates (10 NYCRR §766.12(a)(3)). The principal office in New York State keeps a listing of all personnel (§766.12(a)(1)). Records are made available to DOH promptly on request (§766.12(a)). Records kept electronically are secure, confidential and printable on request (§766.12(b)).

definitions.definition: The file kept for each employee containing the items required by 10 NYCRR §766.11(g) and the agency's own required documents.
Records of an employee's health assessments, immunizations, TB screening and related medical information, kept apart from the personnel record.
The last day the employee works for the agency or the date employment ends, whichever is later.
A current list of all personnel kept at the principal office.

procedures: File creation. The Personnel/HR Coordinator opens a personnel record for each person before the first day of work. A personnel file checklist is attached and updated as documents arrive.

Required contents. Each file holds: application; job description (PER-01); identity verification; employment history and reference verifications; professional licenses or certificates and current registrations; aide training verification and Home Care Registry confirmation (PER-02, PER-03); orientation, competency and in-service records (PER-05); performance evaluations; and employment dates (hire, start of services, position changes, separation).

Time and payment. Time and payment records for each employee are kept as required by §766.11(h), and wage records are kept under PER-09. Payroll staff keep them with the personnel records or in the payroll system, and the Personnel/HR Coordinator can retrieve them on request.

Separate confidential files. Health records (PER-06), influenza status and mask election (PER-07), and CHRC records (PER-04) are kept in locked or access-restricted files apart from the general personnel file. The personnel file holds only a clearance entry showing the requirement was met and the date.

Access. Only the Administrator, the Personnel/HR Coordinator, the RN Director and persons they authorize in writing may open personnel files. Each person who opens a file for review other than routine use signs an access log. Employees may see their own personnel record on written request, in the presence of the Personnel/HR Coordinator.

Electronic records. Electronic personnel files use individual user IDs and passwords, access limits, backup and audit logs. They are kept secure and confidential, and can be printed on request (§766.12(b)). Paper records are kept in locked cabinets in the principal office.

Personnel listing. The Personnel/HR Coordinator maintains a listing of all personnel (name, title, hire date, status and, if separated, separation date) at the principal office. The listing is updated within 5 business days of any hire, change or separation, and is available for DOH review (§766.12(a)(1)). If the agency has a branch office, it keeps a personnel list there (§766.12(a)(2)).

Updating and completeness audit. The Personnel/HR Coordinator audits each file at least annually against the checklist, and an RN or the Administrator audits a sample of files each quarter. Missing items are corrected within 14 days. Results are reported to the QI Committee (GOV-04).

Separation. When an employee separates, the Personnel/HR Coordinator enters the separation date, adds the exit documentation, notifies the Registry designee (PER-03) and CHRC Authorized Person (PER-04), and moves the file to the closed-file location.

Retention. Personnel records, including the separate health and CHRC records, are kept for at least 3 years after separation (§766.12(a)(3)). A record under a pending investigation, claim or DOH request is not destroyed until the matter is resolved and the Administrator approves. Wage and payroll records are kept for any longer period that other law or policy requires (PER-09, REC-03).

Destruction. After the retention period, the Administrator authorizes destruction in writing. Paper is shredded and electronic files are securely deleted. A destruction log lists the name, separation date and date destroyed.

Release of records. Personnel records are released outside the agency only to DOH or other authorized regulators on request, to the employee, or by valid legal process. The Administrator approves each release. References given for former employees are limited to what the Administrator approves.
Review. The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually with the personnel policies (§766.11(a)).

responsibilities.duty: Oversee personnel record-keeping, approve releases and destruction, and make records available to DOH.
Create and maintain files, the personnel listing and the access log, and run annual file audits.
Make sure licenses, competency, supervision and evaluations for clinical staff are filed.
Keep time and payment records as §766.11(h) requires.

responsibilities.role: Designated Registry users and CHRC Authorized Persons
responsibilities.duty: File their confirmations and keep restricted records secure.

documentation: Personnel file with completed checklist
Separate confidential health and CHRC files
Personnel listing kept at the principal office
Access log
Annual and quarterly file audit results
Retention schedule and destruction log

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], especially home care aides, personal care aides and home health aides, and the payroll, scheduling and compliance staff who set, record and audit pay.
policies.purpose: To make sure every caregiver is paid at least the legally required home care aide minimum wage, receives the wage parity benefit portion where it applies, is paid for all hours worked including overtime and travel time, and that the records proving this are kept for the required period.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] pays every home care aide at least the home care aide minimum wage under Public Health Law §3614-f. As of 1/1/2026 that is $19.65 per hour in New York City, Long Island (Nassau and Suffolk) and Westchester, and $18.65 per hour in the rest of the state. These rates rise to $20.00 and $19.00 on 1/1/2027. For Medicaid-funded home care in New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, the agency also meets wage parity under Public Health Law §3614-c. Total compensation must equal the home care aide minimum plus a benefit portion of $2.54 per hour (New York City) or $1.67 per hour (Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester), effective 1/1/2024. In 2026 that is $22.19 per hour in New York City and $21.32 per hour in Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester. The agency completes the annual wage parity certification and obtains an independently audited statement. It keeps wage parity records for 10 years. The agency follows the federal FLSA home care rules (29 CFR Part 552). It pays overtime for hours over 40 in a workweek and pays for all compensable travel time. It does not treat companionship or live-in status as a reason to withhold overtime unless [LABOR COUNSEL/PAYROLL ADVISOR] has confirmed in writing that the exemption lawfully applies to the agency. No employee is asked or allowed to work off the clock.

definitions.definition: A home health aide, personal care aide or other aide who provides home care services and is covered by the home care aide minimum wage law.

The requirement that aides on Medicaid-funded home care in New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester receive total compensation equal to the home care aide minimum wage plus the required benefit portion.

The part of total compensation required by wage parity: $2.54 per hour in New York City and $1.67 per hour in Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester. It may be paid as supplemental benefits or as additional wages as the law allows.
Time an aide spends traveling between clients during the workday, which counts as hours worked.

procedures: Before each calendar year, the Administrator and [PAYROLL MANAGER] review the PHL §3614-f minimum wage and, for wage parity counties, the benefit portion. They update the pay scale and approve it in writing by December 15.
[PAYROLL MANAGER] confirms that no aide's hourly rate is below the minimum for the county where the aide's work is performed. The rate for the county applies on the date the service is delivered.
At hire, Human Resources gives each aide a written notice of the hourly rate, pay day, and any benefit portion. The aide signs it, and it is filed in the personnel record under PER-08.
Human Resources flags each aide's assignments as Medicaid or non-Medicaid and as parity county or non-parity county. Payroll uses this flag to decide when the benefit portion applies.

For parity work, Payroll calculates total compensation each pay period. It confirms that wages plus benefit portion meet or exceed $22.19 per hour (New York City) or $21.32 per hour (Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester) in 2026, and the updated figure in later years.
Aides record hours through the electronic visit verification and timekeeping system described in SVC-13. Payroll pays from verified time and does not round hours in the agency's favor.
Payroll pays all compensable travel time between client visits. Scheduling builds travel time into schedules and does not leave unpaid gaps between back-to-back visits.

Payroll pays one and one-half times the regular rate for all hours over 40 in a workweek, including hours worked for more than one client or location. The regular rate includes required additions to pay.

Aides on extended or live-in shifts are paid in line with the written determination of [LABOR COUNSEL/PAYROLL ADVISOR] on meal, sleep and break time. The agency records the arrangement in the client's schedule and in the aide's file.
Payroll does not allow deductions that would reduce pay below the minimum wage or the required total compensation. Any deduction needs written authorization and review by the Administrator.

Supervisors may not tell, permit or pressure an aide to work unrecorded time. An aide who finds missed or incorrect pay reports it to [PAYROLL MANAGER]. The agency corrects it in the next pay period, or sooner if it is a serious shortfall, and no retaliation follows.

Each quarter, [PAYROLL MANAGER] audits a sample of aide timesheets against paid hours and rates for minimum wage, parity, overtime and travel time. Findings go to the Administrator and to the QI Committee under GOV-04.
For parity work, the Administrator prepares the annual wage parity certification and arranges the independently audited statement through [INDEPENDENT AUDITOR], and files them as required.
The agency keeps all wage parity records for 10 years. Other payroll and time records are kept as stated in REC-03 and PER-08, and not less than the periods required by law.
If an audit or complaint finds underpayment, the agency pays the back wages, corrects the cause, documents the corrective action, and consults [LABOR COUNSEL] about any required notices.
[PAYROLL MANAGER] reviews this policy at least annually with the personnel policies review required under PER-01.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure the agency has the financial resources to pay required wages and receives the annual wage compliance report.
Approves the annual pay scale, signs the wage parity certification, and ensures corrections are made.
Sets rates by county, calculates parity compensation and overtime, pays travel time, performs quarterly audits and keeps records.
Issues pay notices at hire and flags aides and assignments for parity and county.
Builds schedules that account for travel time and prevents unrecorded work.
Record all time accurately and report any pay error right away.

documentation: Annual pay scale approvals showing minimum wage and benefit portion by county
Signed pay rate notices
Timekeeping and EVV records and payroll registers
Overtime and travel time calculations
Quarterly wage audit reports and corrective actions
Wage parity certification and independently audited statement, kept 10 years
Back wage payment records, if any

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors and volunteers of [AGENCY NAME] who have contact with clients, their homes, or their information.
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct and professional boundaries so clients are treated with respect and dignity, their information stays confidential, and they are protected from financial and personal exploitation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires every staff member to treat each client with respect and dignity, as required by 10 NYCRR 766.1(a)(10). Staff must keep client information confidential. All care staff must know the patient rights in 10 NYCRR 766.1 and are oriented to them. Staff may not accept gifts, loans or any financial involvement with clients. Staff do not use client phones, cars or property for personal reasons, and keep personal relationships with clients professional. Staff may not borrow from, lend to, sell to, or enter business dealings with clients or their families. Violations lead to discipline up to termination and may be reported to the appropriate authority. These standards are part of the written personnel policies and job descriptions required under 10 NYCRR 766.11, and are reviewed at least annually.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a caregiver's professional role from a personal, financial or social relationship with a client.
Any loan, gift, sale, purchase, joint account, power of attorney, being named in a will or beneficiary, or handling client money outside of what the plan of care allows.
Anything the client owns or controls, including the home, phone, vehicle, computer, mail, food and belongings.

procedures: Human Resources gives each new employee this policy and the job description at hire. The employee signs an acknowledgment that goes in the personnel record under PER-08.
During orientation under PER-05, the RN Director or designee reviews the patient rights in 10 NYCRR 766.1, respectful care, and this policy. Attendance is documented.

Staff address clients by their preferred name, respect their choices and privacy, and do not use language or behavior that is demeaning. Staff knock and ask before entering rooms or handling belongings.
Staff do not discuss clients with anyone outside the care team or in public places, and do not post about clients, their homes or their care on social media or messaging apps. See CR-04.

Staff politely decline any gift, tip, loan or financial request from a client or family member. If it is hard to decline, the staff member accepts only to avoid offense, tells the supervisor the same day, and the item is returned or handled as the Administrator directs. See CR-05.
Staff do not hold clients' bank cards, PINs, checks or large amounts of cash. They do not sign documents for clients or serve as agent, witness, executor or beneficiary for a client.
Staff do not use a client's phone, car, computer, tools or supplies for personal purposes. They do not use client food or items except as the plan of care allows.
Staff do not bring their own visitors, children or pets to the client's home during work time, and do not sleep during paid hours unless the approved schedule allows it.

Staff keep personal relationships with clients professional. They do not date, romantically or sexually engage with, or request favors from clients. They do not give out personal contact details, and do not take on private paid work with a client outside the agency.
A staff member who is a friend, neighbor or relative of a prospective client tells the supervisor before assignment. The Scheduling Supervisor decides whether the assignment may proceed.

A staff member who sees or suspects a boundary violation, exploitation or disrespect reports it to the RN Director or Administrator right away. Abuse, neglect and exploitation are reported under SAF-01 and unusual events under SAF-02.
The RN Director or Administrator investigates each report promptly, interviews the people involved, protects the client, and documents the findings in a confidential investigation file.
When a violation is confirmed, the Administrator applies discipline from coaching to termination based on severity. Staff who retaliate against someone who reported are subject to discipline.
